headline: South Korea and Iran discuss Hormuz security as Seoul weighs role

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Russian President Vladimir Putin held talks in New Delhi on Friday, meeting shortly before India hosts the BRICS summit. Reuters reported that the agenda covered trade, energy and defense as well as civil nuclear cooperation, fertilizers, manufacturing, railways, steel and critical minerals.

The meeting was the leaders’ second in two weeks and underscored India’s effort to maintain strategic ties with Moscow despite Western sanctions tied to Russia’s war in Ukraine. Russian oil supplied a record 51% of India’s imports in July, although that share later eased as China increased purchases.

Modi reiterated India’s support for diplomacy to end the war and defended the country’s need for reliable energy supplies. The discussions also follow agreements reached during Putin’s December 2025 visit to deepen commercial and defense cooperation.

The talks are developing in the context of the BRICS gathering, where leaders from China and Iran are also expected. Their outcome could affect energy flows, defense procurement and coordination among member countries. Any concrete commitments will depend on formal announcements following the bilateral session and summit meetings.
dek: The leaders met in New Delhi to discuss energy, defense and industrial cooperation as India prepares to host the wider summit.
headline: Modi and Putin hold trade and defense talks before BRICS summit

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Chinese artificial-intelligence developer Z.AI has launched concurrent share and convertible-bond sales that could raise $5 billion, according to term sheets reviewed by Reuters. The package includes a $2 billion Hong Kong share placement and $3 billion of zero-coupon, yuan-denominated convertible bonds.

The Beijing company, formerly known as Zhipu AI, is offering about 21.97 million new shares at HK$714 each, a 10% discount to its previous close. The bonds mature in September 2027 and carry an initial conversion price of HK$892.50, representing a 25% premium.

Z.AI said proceeds would support research and development, computing infrastructure, international expansion, strategic investments, acquisitions and general operations. The two transactions are being marketed together but are not conditional on one another, according to the documents.

The financing illustrates the capital intensity of competing in advanced AI, where model development requires expensive chips, data centers and specialized staff. Z.AI listed in Hong Kong in January and completed another large offering in July. Its latest transaction would give the company additional resources while also increasing the amount of capital investors have committed to China’s AI sector.
dek: The Chinese AI developer is seeking $2 billion from a share placement and $3 billion from convertible bonds for infrastructure and research.
headline: Z.AI launches $5 billion Hong Kong financing package

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Canal+ and Spain’s LaLiga have signed an anti-piracy agreement covering nearly 50 countries where the media company carries league matches. Reuters reported that the partners will combine technical capabilities, coordinate investigations and work together on policy aimed at illegal streaming networks.

The territory spans Europe, sub-Saharan Africa and Haiti. Financial terms were not disclosed. The arrangement extends beyond removing individual streams: both organizations described piracy as a cross-border business supported by increasingly sophisticated distribution systems.

LaLiga said Spanish clubs’ broadcast income fell 5.2% in the 2024-25 season to 1.43 billion euros, even as commercial revenue increased. Canal+ estimated that piracy destroys about 1.5 billion euros of value annually in France, including losses to public tax revenue.

The partnership matters technologically because rights holders increasingly need automated detection, platform cooperation and evidence collection that works across jurisdictions. Illegal services can blend licensed and unlicensed programming and shift infrastructure quickly. Sharing tools and case information could make enforcement faster, though success will still depend on local law, internet providers and courts in each market.
dek: The broadcasters will combine technical tools, investigations and policy work against illegal soccer streams in their shared markets.
headline: Canal+ and LaLiga expand anti-piracy partnership across nearly 50 countries

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Oracle shares were up about 6% in Friday trading after the company reported stronger quarterly results and a $26 billion increase in its revenue backlog, Reuters reported. The reaction reflected renewed investor confidence that demand for AI cloud capacity can support the company’s large data-center buildout.

Oracle’s total backlog reached $664 billion. The company expects roughly half of that amount to convert into revenue over the next three years. Customer prepayments and chips supplied by clients are helping fund some projects, reducing how much capital Oracle must provide directly.

Investors are still watching financing risk. Oracle expects debt to reach about $40 billion this fiscal year, while component costs, project delays and local opposition to new data centers could complicate expansion. The shares had fallen more than 21% in 2026 before Friday’s move.

Reuters said Oracle traded at about 16.9 times expected earnings, below comparable multiples for Microsoft and Amazon. That gap may offer room for recovery if cloud contracts become sales on schedule, but the backlog is not the same as recognized revenue. Execution and funding remain central to the stock’s outlook.
dek: The Friday move followed stronger results and a larger order book, easing some concern about the cost of Oracle’s data-center expansion.
headline: Oracle shares rise as AI cloud backlog adds $26 billion

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Investors pulled a net $32.27 billion from U.S. equity funds in the week through September 9, the largest weekly withdrawal in nine months, according to LSEG Lipper data reported by Reuters. Rising oil prices and persistent inflation readings increased concern that interest rates could move higher.

Large-cap funds accounted for a record $40.44 billion in outflows, while mid-cap products lost $682 million. The pattern was not uniform: multi-cap funds attracted $3.52 billion and small-cap funds added $274 million. Sector funds also received a combined $1.46 billion, led by $1.71 billion for technology strategies.

Money also moved toward fixed income. U.S. bond funds collected $6.56 billion, extending their inflow streak to 21 weeks, with demand concentrated in short-to-intermediate investment-grade and government or Treasury products. Money-market funds, however, recorded $10.41 billion in withdrawals after a much larger intake the week before.

The report captures completed weekly flows rather than real-time market positioning. It nevertheless shows investors reducing broad equity exposure while selectively adding technology and bonds. Upcoming inflation data and the Federal Reserve’s next decision could determine whether that defensive shift persists.
dek: Investors withdrew $32.27 billion in the week through September 9 as oil-driven inflation fears lifted expectations for higher rates.
headline: U.S. equity funds record largest outflow in nine months

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: James Rodriguez has returned to Colombian club soccer, signing with Atletico Nacional on a free transfer through June 30, 2027. Reuters reported that the move is the 35-year-old midfielder’s first professional spell in his home country since he left as a teenager.

Rodriguez most recently played for Minnesota United in Major League Soccer. His career has taken him to 14 clubs in 12 countries, including Real Madrid, Bayern Munich, Porto and Everton. Atletico Nacional adds a globally recognized playmaker with extensive experience in domestic leagues, continental competitions and international tournaments.

The midfielder became an international star at the 2014 World Cup, winning the Golden Boot as the tournament’s leading scorer. Real Madrid subsequently signed him for 75 million euros. Across his club career he has collected 25 trophies, and he has made 131 appearances for Colombia.

The transfer brings Rodriguez back to a league where he developed before beginning his overseas career with Argentina’s Banfield in 2008. Atletico Nacional will now need to integrate his creativity and experience while managing the physical demands on a veteran player approaching the later stage of his career.
dek: The 35-year-old midfielder signed through June 2027, beginning his first spell in Colombia since leaving the country as a teenager.
headline: James Rodriguez returns to Colombia with Atletico Nacional

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: An AI-assisted documentary about Diesel founder Renzo Rosso is screening out of competition at the Venice Film Festival, offering a prominent test of how generated imagery can be used in nonfiction filmmaking. “Be Brave” was directed by Francesco Carrozzini and produced by Lorenzo Mieli.

The film combines interviews and archival material with AI-generated visuals. The synthetic sequences reconstruct moments from Rosso’s childhood and other periods for which no original footage exists, Reuters reported. That makes the technology part of the documentary’s visual language rather than a substitute for every source image.

The approach arrives amid intense debate over whether generative systems can expand creative choices or displace film workers. The filmmakers and Rosso argued that AI should be understood and governed as a tool while maintaining that human judgment remains essential to storytelling.

Venice’s decision to include the film places that debate inside one of cinema’s most established festivals. The screening does not resolve questions about disclosure, authorship or labor, but it gives audiences a concrete work to evaluate. How clearly the generated scenes are distinguished from documented history will remain central to the project’s reception.
dek: “Be Brave” combines interviews and archive material with generated scenes to reconstruct moments from Diesel founder Renzo Rosso’s life.
headline: AI-assisted documentary tests cinema’s boundaries at Venice

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Nashua sewer customers would pay about $3 more per month on average under a three-year rate proposal that advanced from an aldermanic committee. The plan calls for demand and usage charges to increase 7% each January in 2027, 2028 and 2029.

The committee gave the measure a favorable recommendation to the full Board of Aldermen. City officials said the additional revenue would support wastewater operations, debt tied to combined-sewer-overflow work, other system improvements and required reserves as expenses rise.

Officials also reviewed the system’s outstanding accounts. About $1.7 million in sewer bills was listed as unpaid, though roughly $1 million of that total was current and not yet due. The city has placed about 600 liens connected to overdue accounts, according to the meeting report.

The committee vote was 3-1. The proposal still needs approval from the full board before any increase can take effect. If adopted as presented, the phased schedule would spread the adjustment across three years instead of imposing the full change at once, while giving residents a defined timeline for future bills.
dek: A committee backed three annual 7% increases beginning in 2027, sending the plan to the full Board of Aldermen.
headline: Nashua sewer proposal would add about $3 a month for average user

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: New Hampshire’s place in video-game history is receiving renewed attention 60 years after engineer Ralph Baer put his idea for interactive television games on paper. Baer wrote a four-page concept on September 1, 1966, while working for Sanders Associates in Nashua.

The document proposed using a television set for play rather than passive viewing. Back in New Hampshire, Baer worked with engineers Bill Harrison and Bill Rusch to turn the concept into experimental systems, culminating in the wood-grain unit that became known as the Brown Box.

Sanders licensed the technology to Magnavox, which released the Odyssey in 1972. The system is widely recognized as the first commercial home video-game console and helped establish a consumer industry that now spans consoles, computers, phones and online platforms.

Baer continued inventing after the Odyssey and became known as the father of home video games. The Smithsonian preserves his early document, prototypes and workshop materials. The anniversary connects an everyday form of entertainment to engineering work carried out in Nashua and Manchester during the 1960s.
dek: A four-page concept written in September 1966 led to the Brown Box prototype and the first commercial home video-game console.
headline: New Hampshire marks 60 years since Ralph Baer’s home-game blueprint

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Boston and its Public Health Commission are awarding $3.3 million to community health centers as the providers prepare for expected changes in insurance coverage and continued staffing pressure. The money comes from the city’s final year of American Rescue Plan Act funding.

Ten centers will receive $300,000 apiece for existing staff, insurance-enrollment assistance and care programs. A further $300,000 will go to the Massachusetts League of Community Health Centers to support longer-term financial stability, according to the city’s September 10 announcement.

MassHealth projects that new federal work and education requirements beginning in January 2027 could affect around 40,000 Boston residents. City figures place about 40% of that group in Dorchester and Roxbury, with another 20% in Hyde Park, the South End and Mattapan.

The selected providers include NeighborHealth, The Dimock Center, DotHouse Health, Codman Square Health Center and Boston Health Care for the Homeless Program. Community health centers treat patients regardless of insurance status, so the city expects them to absorb more demand if residents lose coverage. The award is one-time funding, separate from Boston’s annual support and other grants.
dek: Ten centers will receive $300,000 each, while a statewide league gets another $300,000 for financial-stability work.
headline: Boston awards $3.3 million to community health centers

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The Boston Zoning Commission has adopted rules for small clean-energy infrastructure, creating a consolidated local permitting process required under the Massachusetts State Climate Act. The framework covers facilities such as solar panels, wind turbines, battery storage and short transmission lines.

The zoning change also sets dimensional and use regulations for battery energy storage systems. State law requires cities and towns to offer the permitting process by October 1, 2026, and Boston said the new rules align with its plans to expand electric-grid capacity.

City planners will next develop design guidelines intended to fit projects into neighborhood settings and address public-space safety. The rules are designed to make requirements more predictable for smaller projects while preserving local review of their placement and form.

Boston’s 2030 Climate Action Plan calls for a 50% reduction in community-wide greenhouse-gas emissions by 2030 and carbon neutrality by 2050. The city says permitting changes are one piece of that strategy, alongside electrification and grid upgrades. Actual projects will still need to meet the new zoning, design and safety standards before construction.
dek: The framework creates a consolidated local permitting process and adds standards for battery storage systems.
headline: Boston adopts zoning rules for small clean-energy infrastructure

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Dr. Selim Suner was at home in North Kingstown with his infant son on September 11, 2001, before events drew him to Rhode Island Hospital and then New York. As leader of the Rhode Island Disaster Medical Assistance Team, he helped mobilize a federal response unit for Ground Zero.

Suner told Ocean State Media that the team included physicians, nurses, paramedics and logistics specialists. Its members initially expected to treat people rescued from the World Trade Center, but New York hospitals had already received the survivors by the time the Rhode Island group arrived.

The mission shifted to caring for rescuers working amid smoke, debris and continuing fires. Suner said the team treated thousands of police officers, firefighters, military personnel, construction workers, search-and-rescue members and working dogs during long shifts at the site.

Now a Brown University physician, Suner reflected on the deployment for the 25th anniversary of the attacks. His account places Rhode Island’s medical-response network within the broader recovery effort and records how quickly local clinicians moved from routine work to a disaster operation hundreds of miles away.
dek: Dr. Selim Suner led a Rhode Island disaster team whose mission shifted from treating survivors to caring for first responders.
headline: Rhode Island doctor recalls medical deployment to Ground Zero

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Providence is bringing the free LUV U BETTER Block Party back to PVDFest on Friday, September 18. The event will run from 5 to 10 p.m. at the Providence Rink, giving the city’s annual arts festival an R&B-focused opening-night program.

Launched in 2015, LUV U BETTER features DJ sets moving across different eras of R&B and soul, with dance music and contemporary hip-hop influences. The city included the event in its newly released full festival schedule.

Saturday’s Plaza Stage program will connect local performers with a national headliner. Earl Bright & Elevated Choir is scheduled to perform at 12:40 p.m. and return during Big Freedia’s 8:30 p.m. set. Providence officials described the collaboration as part of PVDFest’s tradition of pairing city artists with visiting acts.

The block party and stage performances are free. Visitors should check the city’s festival information before traveling for any schedule or access changes. The announced lineup gives residents two distinct entry points: a Friday evening dance party and a broader Saturday slate built around live performance in downtown Providence.
dek: The free R&B event returns September 18, followed by a Saturday program featuring Big Freedia and local performers.
headline: PVDFest brings LUV U BETTER block party back to Providence

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The death toll from a ferry fire off the Philippine island of Palawan rose to 35 on Friday after rescuers recovered 30 bodies from the burned vessel, authorities said. Firefighters were able to board after extinguishing flames that had blocked access since Wednesday night.

The ferry was carrying more than 130 people when fire swept through it near the end of a voyage to Coron. Reuters reported that 43 people had been rescued as of Friday morning. Officials had previously listed 84 people as missing, but the number still unaccounted for after the latest recoveries was not immediately clear.

Survivor accounts collected by the Maritime Industry Authority described two successive explosions before the blaze. The cause has not been established. The vessel also carried motorcycles, an electric vehicle, a forklift, a pickup truck and other cargo, according to the Coast Guard.

The shipowner said it was cooperating with the government investigation. Search teams continued working through the heavily damaged interior as families waited for confirmed identifications and updated passenger counts. The sharp rise in fatalities is a major development from the initial reports of five deaths.
dek: Rescuers recovered 30 bodies after firefighters entered the burned vessel, while the number still missing remained uncertain.
headline: Philippine ferry fire death toll rises to 35

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Health officials in the Democratic Republic of Congo confirmed an Ebola infection in the northwestern province of Sud-Ubangi, far from the center of the country’s ongoing outbreak. The patient was a man who died Tuesday in the town of Gwaka, officials said Friday.

The man had traveled from South Kivu in eastern Congo through Rwanda and Uganda before re-entering Congo and reaching Sud-Ubangi. Congo’s National Institute for Biomedical Research confirmed the positive test, according to Reuters.

Authorities are tracing contacts because the patient used both road and river transport. Local transmission has not been confirmed in Sud-Ubangi, so the province had not yet been added to the official list of affected areas at the time of the report. Its borders with the Republic of Congo and Central African Republic add urgency to surveillance.

The epidemic, first confirmed in mid-May, is Congo’s 17th recorded Ebola outbreak. Government data cited by Reuters listed 6,942 infections and 3,349 deaths. Investigators must now determine where exposure occurred, identify fellow travelers and establish whether the case produced additional infections along the route.
dek: A man who traveled from eastern Congo through Rwanda and Uganda tested positive after dying in northwestern Sud-Ubangi province.
headline: Congo detects Ebola case far from outbreak epicenter

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: More U.S. lawmakers are calling for rules governing advanced artificial-intelligence systems after two Anthropic researchers publicly warned about the possibility of catastrophic harm. The responses came from members of both parties, Reuters reported.

Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon said he had resigned and believed the technology could become an extinction risk before the decade ends. Anthropic scientist Evan Hubinger backed the broader warning. Their statements are forecasts, not documented outcomes, but they intensified an existing policy debate over fast-improving AI agents.

Senate Majority Leader John Thune and Senator Amy Klobuchar are working on legislation addressing high-impact risks. Klobuchar said developers should work with government experts to verify and test systems. A bipartisan House group has separately proposed independent security audits for the most powerful models, with accreditation overseen by the Commerce Department.

President Donald Trump said Thursday that he was not concerned about AI causing human extinction and emphasized competition with China. Anthropic said it would continue testing models for dangerous capabilities in areas including cybersecurity and biology. The competing positions leave Congress debating both the scope and timing of oversight.
dek: Members of both parties cited catastrophic-risk concerns as Senate and House proposals focus on testing and independent audits.
headline: U.S. lawmakers renew AI-rule push after Anthropic researchers’ warnings

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: New Mexico’s Supreme Court said a defense lawyer submitted a murder-appeal brief containing police testimony and witnesses fabricated by ChatGPT. The court fined attorney Stephen Aarons $5,000, held him in contempt and said it would refer the matter to a disciplinary board.

Aarons told Reuters he used ChatGPT to summarize a computer-generated trial transcript and other case material. He acknowledged failing to understand how readily the system could invent facts and described the filing as an honest mistake. OpenAI did not immediately comment to Reuters.

The justices said the brief contained false testimony from wholly invented witnesses. The underlying appeal involves Oscar Renee Sandoval, who was convicted of murdering the mother of his children and sentenced to life in prison. A public defender took over the still-pending appeal on September 2.

Courts have previously sanctioned lawyers over AI-generated citations and misstatements, but this filing extended to purported evidence in a criminal case. The decision underscores that generative tools can produce fluent but unsupported material and that lawyers remain responsible for checking every factual assertion before submitting it to a court.
dek: The state Supreme Court fined a defense lawyer $5,000 after a murder-appeal brief included invented witnesses and testimony.
headline: New Mexico high court says ChatGPT fabricated police testimony

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: U.S. stocks rose Friday morning even after government data showed consumer inflation accelerated in August. At 9:38 a.m. Eastern time, Reuters reported the Dow up 1.23%, the S&P 500 ahead 1.05% and the Nasdaq Composite gaining 1.08%.

The Consumer Price Index increased 0.4% in August after a 0.1% rise in July. Prices were up 3.4% from a year earlier, matching July’s annual rate. The report pushed traders toward higher expectations for a Federal Reserve rate increase, according to futures-market pricing cited by Reuters.

Energy offered some relief to risk sentiment. Brent crude futures fell more than 3%, though they remained above $104 a barrel at the time of the report, while U.S. crude hovered near $100. Elevated oil and Treasury yields had weighed on markets earlier in the week.

All 11 major S&P 500 sectors were positive in early trading, led by technology. The figures are a timestamped market snapshot rather than closing prices. Investors still face uncertainty over inflation, monetary policy and Middle East supply risks as they assess whether the Friday rebound can hold through the session.
dek: Major U.S. indexes gained Friday morning after August consumer prices rose 0.4%, while crude futures pulled back.
headline: Wall Street rises as oil retreats despite hotter inflation

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Coffee traders are preparing large deliveries of Brazilian arabica to ICE exchange warehouses, a move that could more than double certified stocks from 26-year lows and place downward pressure on benchmark prices, Reuters reported.

Market participants are seeking to certify at least 300,000 60-kilogram bags for delivery against the December futures contract. ICE-certified inventories have fallen below 220,000 bags after harvest delays and extreme weather disrupted supplies. More than 62,000 Brazilian bags had already reached depots for grading and quality checks.

Brazilian coffee exports to Belgium jumped 245.3% from a year earlier in August to 31,500 metric tons, government data analyzed by Terra Investimentos showed. Much of ICE’s available arabica is stored in Antwerp, making those shipments an important signal of possible exchange supply.

Certification is not automatic, and it remains unclear how many bags will pass inspection. Even the full expected volume would leave stocks below the roughly 1 million bags traders regard as comfortable. Still, rising inventories can influence algorithmic funds and physical-market expectations, making the delivery pipeline a closely watched commodity-market development.
dek: Traders are seeking to certify at least 300,000 bags of Brazilian arabica as ICE inventories sit near 26-year lows.
headline: Large coffee shipments could rebuild exchange stocks

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Professional football matches in the Netherlands will be abandoned when fireworks are used in the stands under a new safety agreement reported Friday. The policy was reached by the Dutch football federation KNVB, the Public Prosecution Service and Justice and Security Minister David van Weel.

The measure follows an incident during SC Cambuur’s league match against Feyenoord in Leeuwarden last month. Fireworks thrown by visiting supporters left several fans with burns, hearing damage and eye injuries, according to Reuters.

Stopping a match entirely is a stronger response than a temporary suspension. The agreement gives teams, officials and supporters a clear consequence when pyrotechnics are ignited, while authorities work to reduce injuries and disorder inside stadiums.

Implementation details, including how officials will handle identification, announcements and any appeals, were not set out in the initial report. The policy nevertheless changes the immediate calculus for clubs and fans: a single fireworks incident can now end the contest instead of merely delaying it. Dutch football authorities will be watched for how consistently the rule is applied across venues and competitions.
dek: The national federation, prosecutors and justice ministry agreed on the tougher response after fans were injured last month.
headline: Dutch football will abandon matches when fireworks are used

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Thai Formula Two driver Tasanapol Inthraphuvasak escaped without injury after his car crashed and caught fire during Friday practice at Madrid’s new Madring circuit. The accident was the first major crash of the Spanish Grand Prix weekend.

The 20-year-old lost control at turn 19 and spun backward into the barriers. Flames spread through the wreckage, but Inthraphuvasak climbed out of the cockpit without assistance and made his way over the wall, Reuters reported.

Officials stopped the session with a red flag. Marshals took time to reach the car with extinguishers, and the track was not cleared for about 24 minutes. Practice resumed with only six minutes remaining, sharply limiting running for the rest of the field.

The crash occurred before Formula One cars began their own work at the newly built street circuit. Drivers had already raised questions about risks associated with the venue. Inthraphuvasak’s quick exit prevented injury, but the fire and response time will give organizers and racing officials clear evidence to review as the weekend continues.
dek: Tasanapol Inthraphuvasak climbed from his burning car without assistance after hitting the barriers during practice in Madrid.
headline: Thai Formula Two driver escapes fiery Madring crash

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Meredith marked the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks Friday with a public remembrance at Hesky Park and the formal dedication of a new memorial garden at the town’s central fire station.

The town scheduled a procession from the Meredith Fire Department to Hesky Park before the noon ceremony. Police, firefighters and members of American Legion Griggs Wyatt Post 33 joined the observance, which honored the people killed in the attacks and the responders whose service followed.

After the service, participants were invited to march back to the fire station for the garden dedication. The town arranged overflow parking at the municipal lot on Route 3 and shuttle service beginning before the ceremony to help people reach both locations.

The two-part program connected a statewide day of remembrance to a permanent local site. By placing the memorial at the fire station, Meredith created a place where residents can return after the anniversary ceremonies end. The dedication also added another community memorial to the network of New Hampshire observances held Friday from Portsmouth to the Lakes Region.
dek: The Lakes Region community gathered at Hesky Park before a procession to the new memorial garden at the central fire station.
headline: Meredith dedicates September 11 memorial garden

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Flags on New Hampshire public buildings and grounds were lowered to half-staff Friday as the state observed 25 years since the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks.

Gov. Kelly Ayotte issued the directive Thursday, setting the observance from sunrise until sunset on September 11. The order applied across state-owned public facilities and accompanied remembrance events organized by cities, towns, fire departments and veterans groups.

New Hampshire lost 42 people in the attacks, according to anniversary reporting by state broadcasters. Communities held ceremonies throughout the day, including memorial dedications in Dover and Meredith and traditional moments of silence tied to the times the hijacked aircraft struck the World Trade Center and Pentagon and crashed in Pennsylvania.

The flag order did not add new closures or service changes. Its purpose was ceremonial: creating a visible statewide marker while local communities remembered residents, first responders and military members connected to the attacks and their aftermath. Flags were scheduled to return to full staff after sunset Friday.
dek: Flags on state public buildings and grounds were directed to remain at half-staff from sunrise through sunset Friday.
headline: New Hampshire lowers public flags for September 11 anniversary

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Canton unveiled a banner Thursday night honoring Michael Uliano, a hometown Army veteran who was killed in the September 11 attacks 25 years ago.

Uliano grew up in Canton and later worked for a financial firm in the North Tower of the World Trade Center. He was 42 when American Airlines Flight 11 struck the building on September 11, 2001, according to WHDH’s account of the town ceremony.

The banner was placed at a memorial already dedicated to Uliano. During the gathering, participants read the names of people killed in the attacks, lit candles and laid a wreath. The ceremony connected Canton’s local loss to the broader anniversary being marked across Massachusetts and the country.

The tribute gives residents a lasting, visible reminder of Uliano beyond the annual service. It also preserves the personal history of the attacks for younger residents who know September 11 only through family stories, school lessons and public memorials. Canton was among several Massachusetts communities holding observances on Thursday night and Friday.
dek: The town remembered the Army veteran and Canton native who was working in the World Trade Center’s North Tower.
headline: Canton unveils banner honoring September 11 victim Michael Uliano

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: A close friend of Madeline “Amy” Sweeney is remembering the Massachusetts flight attendant’s courage aboard American Airlines Flight 11 on the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks.

Sweeney was working the Boston-to-Los Angeles flight when it was hijacked after departing Logan Airport. Before the aircraft struck the World Trade Center’s North Tower, she contacted American Airlines and relayed critical information about what was happening aboard the plane.

Barbara Bowen, a fellow flight attendant and longtime friend, told WHDH that the two had built a friendship through years of trips and shared family milestones. Bowen had switched crews so she could be home when her son started school, leaving her away from Flight 11 that morning.

Massachusetts later created the Madeline Amy Sweeney Award for Civilian Bravery in her name. The annual honor recognizes people who show exceptional courage while trying to save another person’s life. Friday’s remembrance linked Sweeney’s final call to that continuing public legacy and to Boston’s central role in the history of the attacks.
dek: The Massachusetts flight attendant relayed crucial details about the hijacking before the plane struck the World Trade Center.
headline: Friend remembers Flight 11 attendant Amy Sweeney’s final act of courage

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: A new ramp carrying Route 1 north traffic to Route 37 west is scheduled to open Friday night in Warwick, changing the path for drivers traveling from T.F. Green International Airport toward Interstate 95.

The Rhode Island Department of Transportation said motorists will pass the existing looping ramp and turn left at a temporary traffic signal to enter Route 37 west. The old ramp will close at the same time so crews can continue demolishing the bridge that carries Route 37 over Post Road.

RIDOT urged drivers to slow down and use care while becoming familiar with the new intersection. The agency is rebuilding the interchange so traffic can enter and leave Route 37 through signalized junctions instead of the old ramp-and-bridge layout.

Once the permanent signals are installed, RIDOT plans to synchronize them along the corridor from the airport to Elmwood Avenue. The Friday-night shift is weather-dependent and construction schedules can change, but it represents a significant interim step for one of the state’s key airport-to-highway connections.
dek: Drivers leaving T.F. Green for I-95 will use a temporary signalized left turn as RIDOT closes the old looping ramp.
headline: New Route 1 north ramp to Route 37 west opens Friday night

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Woonsocket drivers face a coordinated series of bridge changes Friday evening as one crossing reopens and two others close for rehabilitation, according to the Rhode Island Department of Transportation.

The Singleton Street Bridge, closed since early June, is scheduled to reopen. Nearby, the Wood Avenue Bridge will close for about six weeks and the River Street Bridge will close through the end of 2026. Both carry local traffic across waterways near major neighborhood intersections.

Wood Avenue traffic will be detoured along Mill Street, Social Street and Diamond Hill Road. The River Street detour uses River Street, Singleton Street, Harris Avenue and Blackstone Street for cars and pedestrians. Trucks will follow a longer route through Blackstone and Millville, Massachusetts, before returning through North Smithfield.

The changes are part of two projects representing a combined $41.8 million investment. RIDOT coordinated the Singleton reopening with the River Street closure to reduce overlapping disruption. All dates remain subject to weather and construction conditions, and drivers should follow posted detour signs.
dek: Singleton Street Bridge is set to reopen while Wood Avenue and River Street bridges close for rehabilitation.
headline: Woonsocket bridge closures and reopening reshape Friday travel

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Israel’s military said Friday that a senior Hamas commander was killed in an airstrike in Gaza a day earlier, as bombing continued despite U.S.-backed efforts to restore a 2025 ceasefire.

Hamas’s armed wing confirmed the death of Mohammed Abdel Salam al-Yazouri. The group said he played a prominent role in planning the October 7, 2023 attacks on Israel that triggered the two-year Israeli military assault in Gaza, Reuters reported.

The Israeli military said the strike targeting Yazouri also killed two other commanders. The initial statement did not provide a broader casualty count or identify the other two people. Reuters reported no immediate additional comment from Hamas beyond its confirmation of Yazouri’s death.

The report is developing because military operations and ceasefire diplomacy remain active, and information from the conflict zone can change rapidly. The announced death removes a figure both sides described as important to Hamas’s armed operations while adding another pressure point to negotiations aimed at limiting renewed fighting.
dek: Hamas’s armed wing confirmed Mohammed Abdel Salam al-Yazouri died in Thursday’s strike, which Israel said killed two other commanders.
headline: Israel says Gaza strike killed senior Hamas commander

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: German federal prosecutors charged seven suspected Hamas members in Berlin on Friday with belonging to a foreign terrorist organization and preparing an attack, including by obtaining weapons.

Prosecutors said the men acted on orders from senior Hamas figures and secured a fully automatic rifle, 13 pistols and more than 700 rounds of ammunition. Authorities allege the weapons were intended for an attack in Germany or Austria around the second anniversary of the October 7, 2023 Hamas-led attacks on Israel.

The intended targets were Israeli representatives, Jewish people or people viewed as pro-Israel, prosecutors said. German domestic intelligence has previously warned that Hamas or affiliated individuals were attempting to establish covert logistics networks in the country for weapons procurement and attack planning.

All seven suspects remain in custody, Reuters reported. The charges move the case into a new legal phase but do not establish guilt; the allegations will be tested in court. German authorities have not announced a trial date in the initial report.
dek: Federal prosecutors say the men obtained firearms and ammunition for a planned 2025 attack in Germany or Austria.
headline: Germany charges seven suspected Hamas members over attack plot

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The Netherlands has signed a letter of intent with Sweden to acquire one Saab GlobalEye advanced surveillance aircraft, adding a national platform designed to monitor air, sea and land over long distances.

The Dutch government said Friday that the aircraft can detect threats including drones and cruise missiles while serving as a flying command center. It can distribute real-time intelligence to aircraft, ships and ground units, linking sensors and operators across multiple domains.

The Netherlands currently relies on NATO’s aging AWACS fleet because it lacks an aircraft for the mission. Delivery of the Dutch GlobalEye is expected in 2031, but the arrangement would give Dutch crews access to Swedish aircraft from 2028 for training and earlier operations.

The purchased aircraft would join a shared pool with three Swedish GlobalEye planes, allowing crews from both countries to use the fleet. The plan reflects rising European demand for airborne early-warning systems as militaries seek better detection of low-flying threats.
The letter of intent is an early procurement step. The initial announcement did not provide a purchase price or a schedule for completing the final contract.
dek: The planned aircraft would monitor air, sea and land, while access to Sweden’s fleet would let Dutch crews begin operating in 2028.
headline: Netherlands moves to buy Saab GlobalEye surveillance aircraft

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The U.S. Export-Import Bank plans to lend nearly $100 million to Africell to expand mobile-network technology sourced from American and allied suppliers, Reuters reported Friday.

Africell, founded in 2001, is the only American-owned telecommunications operator in Africa. It serves about 15 million customers in Angola, Gambia, the Democratic Republic of Congo and Sierra Leone and has used equipment from companies including HP, Nokia, Dell and Oracle.

The financing is part of Washington’s effort to promote alternatives to Huawei infrastructure abroad. Counterpoint Research estimates Huawei holds about 52% of Africa’s 5G infrastructure market. U.S. officials have long raised security concerns about Huawei equipment; the company denies allegations that it could be used to spy on users.

Africell previously received a $100 million U.S. development-finance loan in 2018. The new package would help fund updated network hardware and reinforces the role of public financing in competition over global communications infrastructure, data security and technology standards.
dek: The Export-Import Bank financing would support equipment from American and allied suppliers as Washington counters Huawei’s reach in Africa.
headline: U.S. plans nearly $100 million Africell loan for mobile networks

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: India’s foreign-exchange reserves reached a record $785.7 billion in the week ended September 4, rising by nearly $45 billion from the prior week, central-bank data released Friday showed.

The reserve pool has increased for 10 consecutive weeks and gained almost $120 billion over that span. The Reserve Bank of India attracted $136.3 billion between June 5 and August 31 through measures designed to bring in dollars, including discounted hedging for overseas borrowing and no-cost hedging for banks raising foreign-currency deposits.

Non-resident Indian deposits accounted for $127 billion of the inflows. In the latest week, foreign-currency assets rose by $47.4 billion while the value of gold holdings fell by about $2.6 billion to $113.8 billion.

The larger buffer can strengthen India’s ability to manage currency volatility and external shocks. Bankers told Reuters that intervention to support the rupee likely absorbed some inflows, while analysts noted that hedged deposits also create future obligations in the central bank’s forward book.
dek: Central-bank data show reserves rose by nearly $45 billion in a week after policy measures drew large overseas inflows.
headline: India’s foreign-exchange reserves jump to record $785.7 billion

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: CVC Capital Partners has entered final negotiations to buy the mainland China operations of contact-lens maker Ginko International from EQT, four people familiar with the matter told Reuters.

The potential transaction could value the business at $700 million to $800 million including debt. EQT had sought at least $1 billion, and the financial terms have not been finalized. The talks could still end without an agreement.

Ginko was founded in Taiwan and makes conventional and disposable contact lenses along with lens-care products. Mainland China is its largest sales market. The investment was made in 2022 by Baring Private Equity Asia, which later combined with EQT.

EQT previously agreed to sell the business to Advent International, but that deal fell through. EQT and JPMorgan declined to comment on the latest talks, while CVC and Goldman Sachs did not respond to Reuters. A completed sale would give investors another measure of private-equity appetite for Chinese consumer-health assets.
dek: Sources say a possible deal for the contact-lens maker’s mainland operations could value the business at $700 million to $800 million including debt.
headline: CVC enters final talks for EQT’s Ginko China business

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Ireland’s Eddie Dunbar overtook Santiago Buitrago in the final 500 meters to win Stage 19 of the Vuelta a España on Friday, timing his chase at the end of a hilly day into Estepona.
Dunbar, riding for Pinarello Q36.5, reeled in the Colombian climber after Buitrago had moved into the lead. Teammate Thomas Gloag finished third on the 210.8-kilometer route from Vélez-Málaga.

Spanish rider Enric Mas retained the overall leader’s jersey and will start Saturday’s penultimate stage with an advantage of one minute, 37 seconds over Primoz Roglic. The next test is a 186.8-kilometer mountain route from La Calahorra to Collado del Alguacil.

Dunbar’s late acceleration settled the stage without changing the top of the general classification. Mas now has one major mountain day left before the race reaches its final conclusion, while Roglic must erase a substantial deficit if he is to take the overall lead.
dek: The Irish rider caught Santiago Buitrago with 500 meters remaining while Enric Mas protected the overall lead.
headline: Eddie Dunbar wins Vuelta Stage 19 with late pass

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Swedish defenseman John Klingberg announced his retirement Friday after 700 NHL regular-season games across six teams.

Klingberg, 34, spent his first eight NHL seasons with the Dallas Stars after the club selected him in the fifth round of the 2010 draft. He earned All-Rookie recognition in 2014-15 and was selected for the All-Star Game in 2017-18.

He finished with 443 regular-season points, including 92 goals and 351 assists, during stops with Dallas, Anaheim, Minnesota, Toronto, Edmonton and San Jose. Last season he recorded 27 points in 56 games for the Sharks. Klingberg also produced 43 points in 82 playoff games.

His postseason career included Stanley Cup Final appearances with Dallas in 2020 and Edmonton in 2025. Both series ended in six-game losses. Internationally, Klingberg helped Sweden win consecutive world championship gold medals in 2017 and 2018, adding major national-team success to a long 12-season NHL career as a mobile defenseman.
dek: The Swedish defenseman ends a career that included 443 regular-season points, an All-Star selection and two trips to the Stanley Cup Final.
headline: John Klingberg retires after 700 NHL games

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Franklin residents are encouraging Bradley Minnich to consider running for mayor in the city’s next municipal election. Their encouragement reflects early community interest, although no formal campaign or candidacy has been announced by Bradley Minnich.

Bradley Minnich, 25, is a large land owner in Franklin, NH and a former District Manager of a food chain in neighboring town, Tilton, where he employed dozens of Franklin’s youth over the course of several years. There he led supporting events in collabortion with the Franklin Highschool and neigboring town fairs. Minnich’s acts have led to him being recognized as a "postive influence” from sources.

Franklin’s municipal elections take place in odd-numbered years, typically in early October. The most recent contest, held on October 7, 2025, saw challenger Glenn Morrill defeat incumbent Desiree McLaughlin. Morrill was sworn in as mayor in January 2026 along with newly elected city councilors. Under the city’s charter, the mayor is elected every two years, making the 2027 race the next opportunity for residents to choose Franklin’s chief elected official.

Sources say: "Morrill, a lifelong Franklin resident, campaigned in 2025 on themes of collaboration at City Hall, support for local recreation, and carefully managed capital projects. Since taking office, he has highlighted priorities that include expanding affordable housing options, encouraging local business and industry growth, and establishing a citywide recycling program. Outgoing Mayor McLaughlin used her final council meeting to praise the incoming leadership while expressing concern about the loss of institutional knowledge among newer officials."

Minnich has not released a campaign platform or confirmed whether he intends to enter the race. If he chooses to run, issues facing Franklin—including economic development, housing, municipal services, infrastructure, and the city’s long-term growth—would likely shape the discussion surrounding a potential candidacy. These same topics dominated candidate forums and voter conversations during the 2025 election cycle, when turnout rose noticeably compared with the prior municipal vote.

The expressions of support for Minnich remain informal, and no petition, campaign committee, or organized political group has been announced. The next formal steps would include Minnich deciding whether to become a candidate and completing any filing requirements established for Franklin’s 2027 municipal election. Filing periods for city offices in New Hampshire cities generally open in the summer of the election year, with exact dates set by the city clerk.

Franklin, a city of roughly 8,850 residents in Merrimack County, operates under a mayor–city manager form of government. The mayor works with a nine-member city council (three wards) and appoints or serves on various boards. Local leaders and residents continue to focus on balancing growth with the preservation of Franklin’s character as a small Lakes Region community.
More information about Minnich’s professional background is available on his [LinkedIn profile](https://www.linkedin.com/in/bradleyminnich/).
dek:
Franklin Residents Encourage Bradley Minnich to Consider 2027 Mayoral Run
Several Franklin residents are encouraging Bradley Minnich to consider running for mayor in the city’s next municipal election.
headline: Franklin residents encourage Minnich to run for mayor

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Wind farms across New England generated more than 2,000 megawatts of electricity at the same time Thursday night, setting a regional record, the Concord Monitor reported Friday. The milestone was reached at about 8:30 p.m., according to data from ISO New England, which manages the six-state power grid.

The peak was roughly 30% higher than the previous record set in October. The increase reflects new offshore generation now connected to the grid, including the Revolution Wind project serving Rhode Island and Connecticut and the Vineyard Wind project off Massachusetts. Onshore wind facilities in northern New England also contributed to the total.

A megawatt can supply hundreds of homes, although actual output and demand vary by hour and season. Wind remains one part of a regional mix that also includes natural gas, nuclear, hydroelectric power, solar and imports. Because wind output changes with weather, the grid operator must continuously balance it against other sources. The record nevertheless shows how quickly recently completed projects can alter New England's power supply, particularly during windy off-peak hours when demand is lower.
dek: ISO New England data show regional wind output passed a new threshold Thursday night, helped by recently added offshore projects.
headline: New England wind generation crosses 2,000 megawatts for first time

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Dozens of volunteers gathered at the New Hampshire State Veterans Cemetery in Boscawen on Friday for a National Day of Service marking 25 years since the September 11 attacks, according to the Concord Monitor. Participants cleaned headstones, cleared brush and worked around the cemetery grounds.

Granite United Way coordinated about 130 volunteers across four locations. In addition to the cemetery project, teams served at the New Hampshire Veterans Home in Tilton, worked with Communities for Alcohol- and Drug-free Youth in Plymouth and assembled responder-support kits on the Seacoast. The projects linked remembrance with practical assistance for veterans, first responders and community organizations.

September 11 has been federally recognized as a National Day of Service and Remembrance since 2009. Friday's work offered participants a local way to honor the nearly 3,000 people killed in the 2001 attacks while supporting institutions that serve New Hampshire residents year-round. Organizers emphasized that the anniversary can be observed not only through ceremonies, but also through acts that strengthen local communities and carry the day's lessons into the future.
dek: Granite United Way organized projects at four sites as residents observed the attacks' 25th anniversary with hands-on community work.
headline: New Hampshire volunteers mark September 11 through service

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Massachusetts health officials reported the state's seventh human case of West Nile virus this year on Friday, according to NBC 10. The patient is a man in his 60s who was exposed in Worcester County.

The Department of Public Health continues to classify West Nile risk as moderate across much of Massachusetts. Risk is listed as high in Boston, Brookline, Cambridge, Chelsea, Everett, Malden, Newton, Revere, Somerville, Watertown and Winthrop. Officials have identified 307 mosquito samples carrying the virus in 13 counties, including Bristol County. Eastern equine encephalitis has also been detected in mosquitoes this season.

West Nile is usually spread through the bite of an infected mosquito. Many infected people develop no symptoms, but severe illness can occur, especially among older adults and people with weakened immune systems. Health officials recommend using an EPA-registered repellent, wearing long sleeves and pants when practical, repairing window screens and removing standing water around homes. Residents should also consider limiting outdoor activity from dusk to dawn, when many mosquitoes are most active.
dek: State health officials say a man in his 60s was exposed in Worcester County as mosquito-borne disease risk remains elevated across much of Massachusetts.
headline: Massachusetts reports seventh human West Nile case of 2026

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Raynham police arrested a 17-year-old Friday morning after authorities were alerted to alleged school-shooting and bomb threats posted on an online gaming platform, NBC 10 reported. The teenager's name was not released because the case is in juvenile court.

Police Chief David LaPlante said the FBI notified local investigators after the platform flagged the messages. Officers identified the teenager, searched for weapons and assessed whether there was an immediate danger. Police said the threat was not credible, the teen did not have access to weapons and no weapons were found. Officers nevertheless increased their presence at local schools as a precaution.

The teenager was expected to be arraigned in juvenile court. The allegations have not been proven, and the case remains subject to the protections and procedures of the juvenile justice system. Officials urged families to report concerning online statements rather than attempting to investigate them independently. The incident also highlights the increasingly important role that gaming and social platforms play in detecting threats and quickly forwarding information to law enforcement for assessment.
dek: Police said an FBI alert led to the arrest of a 17-year-old and that investigators found no weapons or evidence of a credible plan.
headline: Raynham teen arrested after online school threat, police say

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Rhode Island held its principal September 11 remembrance Friday at the Rhode Island Veterans Memorial Cemetery in Exeter, 25 years after the attacks, NBC 10 reported. Bells sounded for each of the four hijacked flights as attendees gathered at the cemetery's Wall of Honor.

Rhode Island State Police Colonel Darnell Weaver read the names of nine Rhode Islanders who were killed on September 11, 2001. The ceremony also recognized nine service members from the state who died in wars that followed the attacks. Gold Star families placed a wreath in remembrance, joining veterans, public officials, first responders and community members.

The Exeter observance was among ceremonies across the state, but its setting connected the civilian toll of the attacks with the military service and losses that followed. The anniversary gave families and residents a formal space to remember individual lives while teaching a generation born after 2001 why the day remains central to public memory. Organizers framed the event around service, sacrifice and continued support for families carrying those losses.
dek: Bells marked the four hijacked flights as state leaders and Gold Star families remembered Rhode Islanders killed in the attacks and later wars.
headline: Rhode Island honors September 11 victims at Exeter ceremony

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: NASA astronaut and Brown University alumna Jessica Meir spoke remotely with about 75 Brown students and faculty members from the International Space Station before the start of fall classes, the university said Friday. The private session lasted about an hour and included a tour of the station's Cupola observation module.

Meir described her path to becoming an astronaut and life aboard a laboratory orbiting roughly 250 miles above Earth at about 17,000 miles per hour. Brown planetary scientist Jim Head facilitated the conversation. NASA required specific details to remain private because the event was part of behavioral-health support provided to astronauts on long missions.

Meir graduated from Brown in 1999 and joined NASA's astronaut corps in 2013. During her first mission in 2019, she and Christina Koch completed the first all-woman spacewalk. Meir now commands SpaceX Crew-12, which arrived at the station earlier in 2026 and is expected to return late this year. For students in Providence, the call offered a direct view of scientific work in orbit and a rare chance to ask questions of an alumna leading a current space mission.
dek: The Brown alumna connected with about 75 students and faculty from the International Space Station and gave a guided tour of the orbiting laboratory.
headline: Astronaut Jessica Meir speaks with Brown students from space

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: A passenger train derailed between Rouen and Caen in northern France on Friday evening, injuring about 20 people, French authorities said. The incident occurred near Cleon in Normandy at about 7:54 p.m. local time.

French Transport Minister Philippe Tabarot said 180 passengers were aboard the train. About 140 firefighters were sent to the scene to assist injured passengers and help others leave the train. The prefecture of Seine-Maritime asked the public to avoid the area while emergency crews worked.

Authorities had not immediately released details on the severity of the injuries or the cause of the derailment. Rail service on the corridor was expected to face disruption during the response and investigation. The situation remained developing Friday as emergency teams accounted for passengers and secured the site. Travelers in the region should rely on official rail and local-authority updates before beginning a trip, because early casualty and service information can change as responders complete their work.
dek: Authorities said 180 passengers were aboard the train near Cleon, where 140 firefighters responded Friday evening.
headline: Train derailment in northern France injures about 20

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Saudi Arabia said drones launched from Iraq struck its East-West oil pipeline on Friday, adding another flashpoint to a widening regional conflict. The Saudi foreign ministry announced the attack late Friday without immediately detailing the extent of the damage.

Riyadh said it would not retaliate for now after a request from Iraq's prime minister. The kingdom nevertheless reserved the right to take measures it considers necessary to protect its sovereignty, security and critical facilities. The East-West pipeline carries crude from eastern production areas toward the Red Sea, making it an important alternative route when shipping through the Strait of Hormuz is disrupted.

The announcement came amid attacks affecting energy and shipping infrastructure across the Gulf and Red Sea region. Any sustained interruption to the Saudi pipeline could further complicate oil exports, but authorities had not immediately provided operating or flow data. The source of the drones and responsibility for the attack remained subject to investigation. The situation was developing Friday evening, with attention focused on damage assessments and whether diplomatic efforts can prevent a direct Saudi response.
dek: Riyadh said it would hold off on retaliation after a request from Iraq's prime minister while reserving the right to protect critical facilities.
headline: Saudi Arabia says Iraq-launched drones hit East-West pipeline

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Roblox plans to let developers distribute games created on its platform as standalone apps for mobile devices, PCs and consoles, the company announced Friday at its developers conference. Roblox will supply the underlying technology and services while creators gain another route to reach players outside the main Roblox app.

By the end of 2026, players are also expected to be able to open games in Google's Chrome browser from an Experience Details page without first downloading an app. Support for additional browsers is planned later. Roblox will also allow games to combine online and offline modes, creating room for single-player campaigns and play without a network connection.

The company is expanding its AI-assisted development tools as well. Build, launched in July, lets users create and publish a playable game from a text prompt. Roblox said about 9,000 games have been published with it and that 71% of those creators had not previously used Roblox Studio. A Scene Generator scheduled for later this year will turn text prompts and reference images into functional layouts, while new non-player characters will be able to help playtest games.
dek: New tools will extend Roblox experiences beyond the main app and add offline modes, browser play and AI-assisted creation features.
headline: Roblox will let creators distribute games as standalone apps

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Francisco Partners and KKR have agreed to buy minority stakes in Italian software company TeamSystem from Hellman & Friedman, Reuters reported Friday, citing people familiar with the private transaction. Francisco Partners is set to acquire about 10%, while KKR and other investors would purchase roughly another 5%.

The deal values TeamSystem at between €8 billion and €10 billion, according to the sources. TeamSystem provides accounting, payroll and business-management software to companies and professionals. Its products are closely connected to government electronic-invoicing systems used by small and midsize businesses, a position investors see as difficult for new AI-driven competitors to reproduce quickly.

The transaction is notable after concerns about artificial intelligence contributed to a sharp selloff in software stocks and complicated private-equity exits. It lets Hellman & Friedman return some capital while moving its remaining holding to another fund under its management. The firms and TeamSystem declined to comment to Reuters. Because the terms were described by unnamed sources and the deal was not accompanied by a public closing announcement, final ownership details could still change.
dek: Sources say the private transaction values the Italian business-software provider at between €8 billion and €10 billion.
headline: KKR and Francisco Partners take minority stakes in TeamSystem

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Colgate-Palmolive is exploring the sale of several mass-market personal-care brands, including Softsoap, Irish Spring and Speed Stick, Reuters reported Friday, citing people familiar with the matter. The company is working with Goldman Sachs on the possible divestiture.

The brands under review could bring in more than $1 billion, according to the sources. Colgate's broader personal-care business includes deodorants, soaps, shower gels and skin-care products, but the company is considering selling only part of the unit. Colgate and Goldman Sachs declined to comment to Reuters.

The review comes as major consumer-products companies reshape portfolios in response to tariffs, pressure on household spending and higher energy and input costs. Selling smaller brands can free capital and management attention for products a company considers central to future growth. A review does not guarantee a transaction, and no buyer or timetable was disclosed. Investors will be watching whether a sale proceeds, what valuation the brands receive and how Colgate would use any proceeds. The report concerns a potential deal, not a completed sale.
dek: Sources say the personal-care brands under review could fetch more than $1 billion as consumer groups narrow their portfolios.
headline: Colgate explores sale of Softsoap, Irish Spring and Speed Stick

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Kroger lowered its full-year comparable-sales forecast Friday as slower consumer spending weighed on demand, while leaving its annual profit target unchanged. The grocer now expects identical sales excluding fuel to rise 0.2% to 0.8%, down from its previous 1% to 2% range.

Second-quarter identical sales excluding fuel rose 0.2% in the period ended August 15, compared with 3.4% a year earlier and below the 0.9% estimate compiled by LSEG. Adjusted earnings of $1.09 a share were three cents above the estimate. Kroger said cost controls, e-commerce and retail media helped support profitability despite weaker unit growth.

The company also cited two unusual pressures: a cyclospora outbreak reduced quarterly sales by about 35 basis points, and Medicare drug-pricing changes created an estimated 140-basis-point headwind for pharmacy revenue. Kroger kept its profit guidance as management focuses on sourcing, simpler operations, store openings and faster delivery. The revised sales view adds to evidence that middle- and lower-income shoppers are emphasizing essentials and value as inflation continues to strain household budgets.
dek: The grocer kept its profit outlook after a quarterly earnings beat, but lowered its comparable-sales range amid softer demand.
headline: Kroger trims sales forecast as shoppers pull back

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Katerina Siniakova and Taylor Townsend completed a career Grand Slam as a team Friday, rallying to win the U.S. Open women's doubles final 5-7, 6-0, 6-2 over American wild cards Ashlyn Krueger and Robin Montgomery in New York.

The top-seeded pair recovered decisively after dropping the first set. Early in the second, they won 23 of 27 points to force a deciding set, then consolidated an early break as Townsend held for a 4-2 lead. The turnaround erased a difficult opening frame in which Siniakova double-faulted three times while serving to force a tiebreak.

Siniakova and Townsend had already won Wimbledon in 2024, the Australian Open in 2025 and the French Open earlier this year. Adding the U.S. Open made them champions at all four majors together. The victory was Siniakova's 12th Grand Slam doubles title and made her the first player to complete a team career Grand Slam with two different partners; she previously accomplished the feat with Barbora Krejcikova. For Townsend, the title completed a partnership arc that included a runner-up finish in New York last year.
dek: The top seeds rallied past Ashlyn Krueger and Robin Montgomery in three sets to capture the U.S. Open women's doubles title.
headline: Siniakova and Townsend complete team career Grand Slam

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Michael Kors presented his spring-summer 2027 collection Friday at New York Fashion Week, using graphic stripes, sculptural shapes and bright accents in a show staged at the Museum of Modern Art's sculpture garden.

The collection moved between casual and formal warm-weather clothing, including one-shoulder evening gowns, professional two-piece sets and striped summer dresses. Black and white dominated the palette, with red, green and yellow adding color. Many looks were paired with the designer's signature handbags. Guests included actors Gabrielle Union-Wade, Grace Van Patten and Lea Michele.

The runway arrives during a business reset for the Michael Kors brand. Parent company Capri Holdings lowered its annual revenue forecast last month, citing inventory delays and softer demand for expensive handbags and accessories. Michael Kors revenue fell to $590 million in the quarter ended June 27 from $635 million a year earlier, its 15th consecutive quarter of declining sales. Capri has reduced promotions, updated stores and invested in new products as it tries to rebuild full-price demand. New York Fashion Week runs through September 15.
dek: The designer's spring-summer 2027 collection drew on the Museum of Modern Art sculpture garden with crisp shapes and vivid color.
headline: Michael Kors brings graphic stripes to New York Fashion Week

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Two teenagers have been charged in connection with the fire that badly damaged Kimball Castle in Gilford last year, the New Hampshire State Fire Marshal announced Friday. Joshua Pittman, 18, of Dover, faces a felony conspiracy-to-commit-arson charge and misdemeanor criminal trespass. Peyton Eastman, 19, of Portsmouth, faces felony arson and misdemeanor criminal trespass.

The August 27, 2025, fire was treated as suspicious after flames swept through the historic stone property. Investigators said the building was damaged so severely that demolition was expected. The castle, built in the late 1890s and listed on the National Register of Historic Places since 1982, is a familiar landmark overlooking Lake Winnipesaukee.

Authorities arrested Pittman on September 1 and Eastman on September 2 before announcing the charges Friday. Both were released on personal recognizance and are scheduled for arraignment October 8 in Laconia District Court. The filings are accusations, and the defendants are presumed innocent unless proven guilty. Officials did not announce a motive or disclose additional details about how investigators connected the two teenagers to the fire.
dek: State fire investigators announced felony charges against two teenagers more than a year after flames badly damaged the historic Lake Winnipesaukee landmark.
headline: Two teenagers charged in fire that damaged historic Kimball Castle

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: New Hampshire colleges and universities generated an estimated $17.1 billion in statewide economic activity and supported 114,262 jobs, according to a 2025 report from the New Hampshire College and University Council cited by the Concord Monitor. The report also attributed $636 million in state and local tax revenue to the higher-education sector.

The statewide picture spans 22 institutions serving more than 320,000 students, including online enrollment, with roughly 66,000 students based in New Hampshire. Enrollment is not moving evenly. The University of New Hampshire reported 2,471 first-year deposits for its incoming class, nearly 4% above last year, while out-of-state deposits rose 7% and in-state deposits remained steady.

Smaller campuses continue to face pressure. Keene State College enrollment has declined from about 5,000 students in 2015 to roughly 2,800 this year, and the school is addressing a $3.3 million deficit with staffing reductions. New Hampshire also ranks last nationally in public higher-education funding, while the current state budget reduces four-year public-campus support by 14%. Community-college early-college programs now serve more than 11,000 students annually and receive $3 million in state support.
dek: A new statewide assessment puts higher education's economic impact at $17.1 billion while highlighting sharply different enrollment trends across campuses.
headline: New Hampshire colleges report $17.1 billion impact amid enrollment shifts

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Boston police arrested a 35-year-old Dorchester woman after a stabbing near 950 Blue Hill Avenue on Thursday evening. Authorities identified the suspect as Jasmine Noiles and said she faces assault and battery charges, including assault and battery causing serious bodily injury.

The Boston Police Department said officers responded to the Blue Hill Avenue area and made the arrest in connection with the reported stabbing. NBC10 Boston reported the case Friday as detectives continued reviewing the circumstances. Officials had not released the injured person's name or a detailed account of what led to the encounter in the initial public notice.

Noiles is expected to be arraigned in Boston Municipal Court, where prosecutors will present the allegations and a judge will determine release conditions. The charges are accusations, and she is presumed innocent unless proven guilty. Police did not immediately disclose whether the people involved knew one another or provide an updated condition for the injured person. Anyone with information can contact Boston police; anonymous tips may be submitted through the department's CrimeStoppers program.
dek: Boston police arrested Jasmine Noiles, 35, after a Thursday-evening stabbing near 950 Blue Hill Avenue.
headline: Dorchester woman charged after Blue Hill Avenue stabbing

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: An 83-year-old man was arrested during a joint police operation at Cathedral Pines, a wooded recreation area shared by Essex and Manchester-by-the-Sea. NBC10 Boston reported Friday that the operation followed complaints about inappropriate activity in the area, including a report that someone had grabbed another visitor and behaved lewdly.

Police from both communities assigned plainclothes and uniformed officers to the property. Authorities said the man was taken into custody after propositioning a detective during the patrol. His name and the specific charge were not included in the initial public report, and officials did not say whether he was suspected in the earlier grabbing allegation.

The arrest comes as the two departments increase their presence at Cathedral Pines in response to visitor concerns. Police said the patrols are intended to deter misconduct and keep the public recreation area accessible. The reported conduct remains under investigation, and an arrest is not a finding of guilt. Visitors who witness threatening, unwanted or illegal behavior should leave the immediate area when safe and contact local police with the time, location and description of what occurred.
dek: A joint Essex and Manchester-by-the-Sea patrol followed complaints about inappropriate activity in the wooded recreation area.
headline: Joint patrol leads to arrest at Cathedral Pines recreation area

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Cranston police arrested two New York men early Friday after officers recovered about 100 gallons of used cooking oil that authorities say had been taken from a local restaurant. Anyeson Veras Martinez, 26, and Steven Velez Toribio, 29, were each charged with larceny under $1,500.

Police said a Flock license-plate reader alerted officers at 1:57 a.m. to a white 2018 Ford Transit with a Pennsylvania plate associated with cooking-oil thefts. A second alert placed the van near Route 37. An officer located it at PJ's Pub on Pontiac Avenue and stopped it at about 2:20 a.m.

According to police, the van smelled of cooking oil and contained residue, two large containers, a hose and a pump. Investigators estimated the recovered oil's value at about $200. Used restaurant oil can be processed into biofuel and other products, giving it a resale value that has made storage tanks a theft target. The charges are allegations, and both men are presumed innocent unless proven guilty. Police did not immediately say whether the case is connected to other reported thefts.
dek: A license-plate reader alert led officers to a van carrying about 100 gallons of used restaurant oil, police said.
headline: Two men charged after Cranston cooking-oil theft

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Firefighters from East Providence and Rehoboth completed a 110-story memorial stair climb Friday at City View Manor, honoring first responders who died during the September 11 attacks. It was the first year the neighboring Rhode Island and Massachusetts departments organized the climb together.

Participants climbed the building's 11 flights ten times while wearing nearly 60 pounds of protective equipment. The repeated ascent matched the height of the World Trade Center towers and gave the public a physical reminder of the conditions firefighters faced. Families and community members gathered at the property to watch and support the crews as they worked through the heat.

Organizers said they hope the joint climb becomes an annual tradition. Donations associated with the event support the Tunnel to Towers Foundation, which assists injured service members, first responders and families of those killed in the line of duty. The collaboration also linked two local departments whose members regularly train for high-rise rescues and other emergencies. Friday's event focused on remembrance, shared service and the continuing impact of September 11 on fire departments across New England.
dek: Crews from East Providence and Rehoboth climbed the equivalent of 110 stories in nearly 60 pounds of gear.
headline: East Providence and Rehoboth firefighters complete 110-story memorial climb

author: NorthEast News Desk
