dek: Forensic teams are processing remains recovered from the MV June Aster after the death toll reached at least 35 and more than 50 people remained missing.
headline: Philippines begins identifying ferry-fire victims as dozens remain missing

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Chinese President Xi Jinping arrived in New Delhi on Saturday for the BRICS summit and a scheduled meeting with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Indian television channels reported. It is Xi’s first visit to India in seven years and turns days of planning into a direct diplomatic test for Asia’s two most populous countries.

The leaders are expected to meet Saturday evening. Their talks come after a gradual effort to stabilize relations damaged by the 2020 border clash in the Himalayas, which killed 20 Indian soldiers and four Chinese troops. Xi and Modi have met twice in the past three years, but unresolved border and strategic tensions continue to shape the relationship.

The BRICS gathering provides a broader setting for discussions among major emerging economies, while the bilateral meeting offers a measure of whether recent contacts can produce practical progress. No outcome had been announced at the time of Xi’s arrival. Attention will center on the language used after the talks and whether the two governments identify concrete steps on border management, trade or diplomatic engagement.
dek: The Chinese president’s first visit to India in seven years moves a planned meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi from preparation to a closely watched diplomatic test.
headline: Xi arrives in Delhi for BRICS summit and Modi talks

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Artificial-intelligence startup Discovery Loop is seeking new funding at a valuation of about $50 billion, Business Insider reported, citing people familiar with the discussions. The terms could change and there is no guarantee the talks will result in a transaction, making the figure an indication of investor negotiations rather than a completed valuation.

The reported target represents an unusually rapid increase for a company launched this year. Discovery Loop was in talks last month to raise about $1 billion at a valuation near $10 billion, according to the report. The startup is structured as a public benefit corporation and is focused on using machine learning for scientific and engineering research.

Its founding team includes prominent artificial-intelligence and engineering leaders, including longtime Google researcher Jeff Dean. The fundraising effort reflects continued investor appetite for teams with established AI credentials even as spending requirements and commercialization timelines remain uncertain. Discovery Loop did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment, and no investors or final financing amount were confirmed.
dek: The young AI research startup is pursuing a sharp valuation increase, according to Business Insider, though terms could change and a deal is not assured.
headline: Discovery Loop seeks funding at reported $50 billion valuation

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Apple’s first foldable phone, the iPhone Duo, will start at $1,999 in the United States, placing it at the high end of an already small smartphone segment. The largest-storage version is priced at $3,199. Apple demonstrated apps including Zoom, Slack and Netflix using the expanded display and positioned the device as a personal hub for artificial intelligence.

The launch gives Apple a new form factor but leaves a central question about the size of the audience willing to pay the premium. IDC expects foldables to account for less than 3% of global smartphone shipments in 2026 and 2027. Counterpoint Research estimated Apple could sell about 6 million units by year-end, roughly a quarter of the foldable segment.

Samsung currently holds about 40% of the foldable market, giving Apple an established rival and a benchmark for durability, software and everyday usefulness. Omdia projects 22.3 million foldable shipments worldwide this year. Apple’s entry could expand consumer awareness, but its initial price means the Duo’s early performance will test whether large-screen multitasking and AI features are compelling enough to move foldables beyond a niche.
dek: Apple is pitching its first folding phone as a premium personal AI device, but analysts question how broad the audience will be at its launch price.
headline: Apple’s $1,999 iPhone Duo tests the foldable market

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: JPMorgan Chase ended lending activity for Situational Awareness after leveraged bets tied to artificial intelligence produced large losses and brought the hedge fund close to collapse, a person familiar with the matter told Reuters. The fund liquidated most of its public-equity holdings to Citadel after a global rout in chip stocks exposed the scale of its borrowing.

Situational Awareness was launched in 2024 by former OpenAI researcher Leopold Aschenbrenner and built concentrated positions across the AI ecosystem. The fund told investors its portfolio fell 67% in July, when the selloff generated a margin call and pressure to raise capital or dispose of holdings. JPMorgan was one of its key lenders before notifying the fund that the relationship would end.

Other banks, including Goldman Sachs, Citigroup and Bank of America, remain active brokers for the fund, and it recently began working with Clear Street. The episode illustrates how leverage can amplify a crowded technology trade when markets reverse. Reuters said the banks declined to comment and Situational Awareness did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
dek: The bank ended its lending relationship after leveraged artificial-intelligence bets produced steep losses, a source familiar with the matter told Reuters.
headline: JPMorgan curbs lending to AI-focused Situational Awareness fund

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: India’s market regulator has proposed changing how settlement prices are set for derivatives on expiry days after sharp closing moves raised concerns about the new auction process. The Securities and Exchange Board of India is seeking public comment on two alternatives for calculating the final value used to settle expiring contracts.

One option would blend prices from the final 30 minutes of regular trading with those from the 10-minute Closing Auction Session. The other would return, for at least a year, to using only the final 30 minutes of normal trading and exclude the auction. SEBI also proposed limiting cancellation of orders placed more than 1% away from the indicative price and shortening the post-close window from 10 minutes to five.

The regulator said the auction has generated volatility around expiry and is considering withholding an indicative index close during that period. The consultation does not immediately change settlement rules, and market participants have until October 3 to submit comments. The final approach will matter to exchanges, brokers and investors because small closing-price moves can materially affect large derivatives positions.
dek: SEBI is consulting on two alternatives after sharp end-of-day swings raised concerns about how expiring contracts are settled.
headline: India proposes overhaul of derivatives expiry pricing

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Uganda’s Tooro Kingdom prepared to bury King Oyo Nyimba on Saturday in Fort Portal after days of dispute over who should succeed him. Royal guards led a procession carrying his flag-draped casket from the palace to St. John’s Cathedral, where hundreds of mourners and senior government officials gathered before the burial at the royal tombs.

Oyo became internationally known in 1995 when he took the throne at age 3. He died in the United States in late August at 34 while receiving cancer treatment. During his reign he served as a United Nations goodwill ambassador and promoted efforts against HIV and AIDS, while the kingdom remained an important source of cultural identity in western Uganda.

A royal clan committee selected Oyo’s cousin Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma as king, but Oyo’s immediate family said a previously unknown son should inherit under the late monarch’s will. Supporters of Kijanangoma questioned whether enough information about the purported son had been produced. Ugandan authorities strengthened security as the kingdom moved ahead with the funeral and its traditional succession rites.
dek: The monarch who took the throne at age 3 is being laid to rest in Fort Portal after his death at 34 and a contested choice of successor.
headline: Uganda’s Tooro Kingdom buries King Oyo amid succession dispute

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Aryna Sabalenka and Elena Rybakina will meet in Saturday’s U.S. Open women’s final, pairing two of the sport’s biggest servers in a championship match with rankings and history attached. Sabalenka is seeking a third consecutive title in New York, a run no woman has completed since Serena Williams won three straight through 2014.

Rybakina is set to become world No. 1 when the rankings are updated Monday, regardless of the final’s outcome. The match will be the third Grand Slam final between the two. Sabalenka won their 2023 Australian Open title match, while Rybakina reversed that result at this year’s Australian Open.

Sabalenka leads their head-to-head series 10-7, but the margins have often been narrow because both players can shorten points with first-strike tennis. The contrast is less about power than temperament and execution under pressure: Sabalenka brings an expressive, aggressive style, while Rybakina is known for a more restrained presence. Their latest meeting will decide the season’s final major and add another chapter to one of the tour’s defining rivalries.
dek: Aryna Sabalenka seeks a third consecutive New York title against Elena Rybakina, who is due to become world No. 1 after the tournament.
headline: Sabalenka and Rybakina set heavyweight U.S. Open final

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Freshman Tasha Udebhulu scored her first collegiate goal with a little more than 15 minutes remaining, lifting Dartmouth women’s soccer to a 1-0 win over Holy Cross at Burnham Field. The result gave the Big Green a second consecutive victory and stopped a Crusaders team that arrived in Hanover on a four-game winning streak.

The decisive chance began when an attempted clearance by the Holy Cross goalkeeper deflected off Udebhulu just outside the penalty area. The Guildford, England, native collected the loose ball, moved around the goalkeeper and eluded recovering defenders before finishing for the only goal of the match.

Dartmouth improved to 4-1-2 after creating more pressure following halftime. Holy Cross held a 6-3 advantage in shots during the opening half, but the Big Green produced eight attempts in the second. The late breakthrough rewarded that shift while the Dartmouth defense preserved the shutout. The team’s next scheduled match is a Sunday home date with Colgate.
dek: Freshman Tasha Udebhulu broke a scoreless tie late at Burnham Field, giving the Big Green a 1-0 victory and a second straight win.
headline: Udebhulu’s first college goal lifts Dartmouth over Holy Cross

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: A crowd gathered at the Claremont Visitor Center on Friday for a memorial stair climb marking 25 years since the September 11 attacks. Organized by Claremont Parks and Recreation, the event gave participants a route designed to equal 110 stories, the height of each World Trade Center tower.

The group ranged from children as young as 5 to people in their 80s, and some walkers brought dogs. Two firefighters from nearby Weathersfield climbed in full turnout gear. Participants could choose their own distance and pace rather than complete the entire challenge, while the most demanding option called for 20 loops of 110 stairs in gear or a weighted vest.

The event honored the nearly 3,000 people killed in the 2001 attacks, including hundreds of firefighters and other emergency personnel. Fire Chief Jim Chamberlin told the gathering that the community’s continued remembrance a quarter-century later was both humbling and a hopeful reflection of Claremont. The climb combined a demanding physical tribute with an accessible community observance.
dek: Residents of many ages completed routes modeled on the World Trade Center’s 110 stories during the city’s 25th-anniversary remembrance.
headline: Claremont stair climb honors September 11 victims

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: A federal judge in Boston on Friday blocked the government from continuing to ask applicants for career civil-service jobs to write essays explaining how they would help advance the president’s policies and executive orders. U.S. District Judge George O’Toole issued the ruling in a case brought by three unions representing public employees.

O’Toole concluded that the unions were likely to show the question infringed applicants’ speech rights and violated the Administrative Procedure Act. His decision noted that federal civil-service law bars hiring decisions based on political affiliation. The unions said more than 70,000 job postings had included the question, covering positions as varied as air traffic control specialist, crane operator and nuclear materials courier.

The Office of Personnel Management did not immediately comment on the ruling. The agency previously said the response was optional and that political beliefs could not be used in hiring decisions. The question was adopted as part of a hiring plan developed after a January 2025 executive order. The order halts the essay requirement while the unions’ challenge proceeds.
dek: U.S. District Judge George O’Toole halted a question asking civil-service applicants how they would advance presidential policies and executive orders.
headline: Boston judge blocks federal hiring essay question

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The Kansas City Royals converted an early three-run lead into a 3-2 victory over the Boston Red Sox on Friday night at Fenway Park. Kansas City scored in the first and twice in the third, then held Boston to one hit over the final four innings to open the three-game series with a win.

Carter Jensen doubled twice and drove in a run, while Salvador Perez added two hits and an RBI. Seth Lugo allowed two runs on seven hits over five innings, striking out seven, and four relievers protected the advantage. Steven Cruz retired the side in order in the ninth for his seventh save.

Boston’s Mickey Gasper hit his ninth home run of the season in the fifth. Wilyer Abreu followed later in the inning with an RBI double off the Green Monster, cutting the deficit to one, but Lugo ended the threat with consecutive strikeouts. Sonny Gray allowed three runs in six innings for Boston. The Red Sox fell to 80-68 and have lost three straight after a five-game winning streak.
dek: Kansas City scored three times in the first three innings, then relied on its bullpen to hand Boston a third consecutive loss.
headline: Royals hold off Red Sox 3-2 at Fenway Park

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Brown field hockey rallied from two goals down in the fourth quarter and defeated Boston University 5-4 after a shootout Friday at Goldberger Family Field. The Bears trailed 4-2 with 13:40 remaining before Sophia Clark and Kate Siedem scored 59 seconds apart to force overtime.

Neither team scored in the extra period, sending the match to a shootout. Kiersten Smith, Julia Lattuada and Mia Karine Myklebust converted for Brown, with Myklebust producing the deciding goal in a 3-2 shootout advantage. Goalkeeper Ellie Parker matched a career high with 10 saves after Boston University controlled long stretches of possession.

Grace Almeida, Smith, Siedem and Clark accounted for Brown’s four regulation goals. The Terriers had opened a 2-0 lead in the second quarter, and later moved ahead 4-2 early in the fourth before the comeback. Brown improved to 2-1 and earned its second straight victory. The Bears are next scheduled to travel to Fairfield for another nonconference match.
dek: The Bears tied the game in the fourth quarter and won a shootout 3-2, with Mia Karine Myklebust supplying the deciding attempt.
headline: Brown field hockey erases two-goal deficit to beat Boston University

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Providence College volleyball opened its home schedule with a straight-sets victory over Manhattan University on Friday night at Alumni Hall. The Friars won 25-14, 25-13 and 25-9 in the opening match of the 21st annual Friar Classic, improving their early-season record to 6-1.

Macy Taylor and Sophia Adkins paced the Providence offense with nine kills apiece. The Friars finished with 40 kills as a team and held Manhattan to a negative attack percentage. Setter Miller McDonald added five service aces and recorded a .957 serving percentage, helping Providence control extended stretches in each set.

Providence used six-point runs in the opening set to create separation, then led the second set from start to finish. The Friars built a 10-4 advantage in the third and stretched the margin to double digits before closing the sweep with back-to-back points. Providence is scheduled to continue the tournament Saturday with matches against Stonehill in the afternoon and Holy Cross in the evening.
dek: The Friars won all three sets by double digits to begin the Friar Classic, improving to 6-1 behind a balanced attack and strong serving.
headline: Providence volleyball sweeps Manhattan in home opener

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: BRICS negotiators reached agreement on a joint declaration Saturday as leaders began summit talks in New Delhi, according to four sources familiar with the discussions. The reported deal is a significant test of the expanded group’s ability to maintain consensus while members Iran and the United Arab Emirates remain divided over the Gulf conflict.

The sources said the draft was unlikely to name any country but would condemn unilateral aggression. Leaders were expected to consider the document later Saturday. India’s foreign ministry did not immediately comment on the reported agreement. Host Prime Minister Narendra Modi opened the summit by urging members to turn their shared positions into concrete results and renewed his call for reform of the United Nations Security Council.

A BRICS foreign ministers’ meeting in May ended without a joint statement because members could not bridge their differences. The declaration therefore represents a diplomatic advance even before final approval. BRICS is also seeking greater influence over international financial and trade institutions. Details may change as leaders debate and approve the final text.
dek: Negotiators agreed on language that sources said would condemn unilateral aggression without naming a country, with leaders expected to consider it Saturday.
headline: BRICS reaches joint-declaration deal despite Middle East divisions

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman asked President Donald Trump for military assistance against Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis, three sources familiar with the matter told Reuters. The sources said the leaders spoke at least twice Thursday and that the United States did not agree to conduct strikes, instead offering help with intelligence sharing and targeting.

The White House did not confirm the calls. A senior administration official said the United States remained in continuous dialogue with Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s government, with a focus on freedom of navigation and support for regional partners. Saudi Arabia’s government media office did not immediately respond to Reuters’ request for comment. Two sources also said the head of U.S. Central Command traveled to Saudi Arabia for talks Thursday.

The reported request came as Houthi forces advanced along Yemen’s Red Sea coast and reached Perim Island in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, according to Yemeni government sources. Control near that shipping corridor could add pressure to energy and cargo routes already strained by reduced traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. The situation remains fluid.
dek: Three sources told Reuters that Washington declined direct strikes while offering intelligence sharing and targeting assistance as Red Sea tensions rose.
headline: Saudi crown prince sought U.S. military help against Houthis, sources say

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Boston Logan International Airport has installed eight artificial-intelligence-powered holograms to help travelers find gates, restaurants, baggage claim and other locations. The assistants, named “Amelia” after aviation pioneer Amelia Earhart, are positioned across every terminal, both before and after security checkpoints.

The system can provide step-by-step directions in several languages and display a QR code so travelers can carry those instructions on their phones. Airport officials said Amelia can be programmed with thousands of locations and described the deployment as the largest use of this hologram technology at any airport. Logan expects the units to handle about 100,000 interactions during their first year.

Massport says the goal is to supplement its customer-service staff, not replace employees. The current version is focused on common wayfinding questions, while a planned second phase would make the system more conversational and capable of answering a broader range of requests. The installation gives Logan a visible test of how generative AI and projection technology can be integrated into busy public spaces.
dek: The airport’s new “Amelia” assistants offer directions in every terminal and can send step-by-step routes to travelers’ phones by QR code.
headline: Boston Logan deploys eight multilingual AI holograms

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Anthropic’s planned expansion in Cambridge is arriving alongside renewed warnings from current and former artificial-intelligence researchers about the risks posed by increasingly capable systems. The company plans a larger presence at One Kendall Square, placing more of its workforce near the universities and laboratories that anchor the region’s technology sector.

NBC10 Boston reported that former Anthropic and OpenAI researcher Jacob Coxon this week warned that frontier models could become dangerous on a short timeline. Other experts have focused on the growing autonomy of AI agents, which can plan and perform multiple steps with less human direction. The concerns include whether developers and regulators can test systems thoroughly enough before broad deployment.

Anthropic said Cambridge is a natural base because of its scientific and academic institutions. The local expansion also makes the national AI-safety debate more immediate for Massachusetts, where residents interviewed by NBC10 expressed both concern and optimism. A recent NBC News poll cited by the station found broad public unease about AI and a belief that government oversight has not kept pace with the technology.
dek: The company is preparing a larger Kendall Square presence as current and former industry researchers raise concerns about increasingly autonomous systems.
headline: Anthropic’s Cambridge expansion draws fresh AI-safety scrutiny

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: United Arab Emirates stock markets closed higher Friday as a sharp weekly rise in oil prices offset continued concern about shipping disruptions in the Middle East. Dubai’s benchmark advanced 0.6% after two losing sessions, while Abu Dhabi’s index edged up 0.03% for a fourth consecutive gain.

Emirates NBD, Dubai’s largest lender, rose 4.2%, and district-cooling company Empower gained 1.9%. In Abu Dhabi, investment firm Two Point Zero added 3.6%, Adnoc Logistics & Services climbed 2.9%, and NMDC Group gained 3.5%. Declines in Fertiglobe and First Abu Dhabi Bank limited the broader index’s advance.

The figures are Friday closing data, not live prices. Crude was on course for a weekly gain of more than 7% as attacks and reduced vessel traffic raised concern about persistent supply constraints. For the full week, Abu Dhabi’s benchmark gained 1.4% and Dubai’s added 1%, according to LSEG data cited by Reuters. The moves show investors balancing stronger energy-linked revenue expectations against escalating regional risk.
dek: Dubai’s benchmark rose 0.6% at Friday’s close, while Abu Dhabi edged higher for a fourth session amid pressure on regional shipping routes.
headline: UAE shares finish higher as oil-supply concerns support markets

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Canadian supermarkets are changing labels and supply relationships as more shoppers seek domestic products and avoid U.S. goods amid a renewed trade dispute. Independent grocers are sourcing produce from Canada and countries including Mexico, Morocco, South Africa, Spain, Brazil and Honduras, according to retailers interviewed by Reuters.

Vince’s Market, which operates four stores in the Greater Toronto Area, said about 90% of its produce is now Canadian. The chain switched strawberry sourcing to Quebec and reduced advertising spending as the procurement changes increased operating pressure. Loblaw brought back large maple-leaf signs in fresh-food sections and reintroduced tags identifying products affected by tariffs. Metro said it would continue prioritizing Canadian goods.

The shift matters because Canada remains heavily dependent on imported fruits and vegetables. The United States supplies more than half of Canadian fresh-vegetable imports, although its share fell to 62.6% in July from 69% in July 2023. Ottawa is also planning about C$3 billion in spending on greenhouses and vertical farms over a decade, seeking to reduce seasonal supply constraints.
dek: Retailers are expanding origin labels and finding alternatives to U.S. produce as consumer preferences and trade tensions alter supply decisions.
headline: Canadian grocers shift sourcing as buy-local boycott reshapes shelves

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The Tampa Bay Rays and Milwaukee Brewers became the first Major League Baseball teams to secure 2026 postseason places Friday, clinching in dramatically different fashion. Tampa Bay beat Houston 3-1 on Junior Caminero’s walk-off home run, while Milwaukee overwhelmed Cincinnati 20-0.

Caminero drove a 417-foot homer off Bryan Abreu for his 40th of the season, turning a tie game into a celebration at Tropicana Field. The win guaranteed the Rays a playoff berth with the regular season entering its final stretch. Tampa Bay’s pitching held Houston to one run before the ninth-inning finish.

Milwaukee left little doubt in its clincher. Garrett Mitchell hit a grand slam, William Contreras homered and drove in six runs, and Dustin May allowed two hits over six scoreless innings. The Brewers earned their eighth postseason appearance in nine seasons. With both clubs officially through, attention now shifts to division positioning and the remaining wild-card races as the rest of the field takes shape.
dek: Tampa Bay advanced on Junior Caminero’s walk-off homer, while Milwaukee secured its place with a 20-run rout of Cincinnati.
headline: Rays and Brewers become first teams to clinch MLB playoff berths

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Sanjay Sah was released from a Kathmandu hospital Friday after surviving nine days trapped inside a tunnel at Nepal’s Upper Trishuli 3A hydropower station. Floods and mudslides struck the Bhotekoshi River area and tore through the facility, leaving the 30-year-old mechanical foreman isolated deep inside the mountainside powerhouse.

Sah told Reuters that he had no food and survived by drinking floodwater and water seeping from the mountain rock. He spent long periods with his eyes closed because darkness and debris made movement hazardous. From an opening on the fifth floor of the six-story structure, he shouted in hopes of finding other survivors but heard no response.

Rescuers reached Sah on the 10th day after the disaster. He said thoughts of his wife, young daughter and wider family helped him maintain hope. The rescue provided a rare positive outcome after the late-August collapse of a Himalayan glacier caused widespread destruction across Nepal and China’s Tibet region, where authorities have reported heavy loss of life and thousands missing.
dek: Sanjay Sah said he survived without food by drinking floodwater and seepage before rescuers reached the mountain hydropower station.
headline: Nepal tunnel survivor leaves hospital after nine-day ordeal

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Black Cloud Brewing Co. is giving a familiar downtown Keene taproom a new identity, combining beer made on site with a food menu built around thin-crust pizza. The brewery opened earlier this year at 100 Main Street in the former Modestman Brewing space after that business closed last summer.

NBC10 Boston reports that former Modestman employees helped shape the new operation, which includes counter service, group seating, a quieter rear patio and views of brewing equipment. The beer list spans a hazy New England IPA, a German-style black lager, a fruited sour, a pale ale and an American red ale, offering a wider range than a single-style taproom.

The kitchen uses a high-temperature ventless conveyor oven to produce Neapolitan-style pizza with a charred thin crust. Locally sourced toppings, vegan options and a hot-maple drizzle made with syrup from Saxtons River, Vermont, give the menu a regional accent. Pickled vegetables, olives, pretzel bites, popcorn and salads round out the food choices. The opening keeps brewing activity in a prominent Main Street location while adding another gathering place for residents, visitors and the city’s college community.
dek: Former Modestman employees helped create the downtown taproom, where locally accented pizza shares the billing with a varied beer list.
headline: Black Cloud Brewing gives Keene taproom a new identity

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: West Lebanon’s Route 12A dry bridge is scheduled to close at 7 a.m. Monday, September 14, beginning a yearlong demolition and replacement project on one of the city’s busiest local connections. The 77-year-old span links South Main Street with the Route 12A shopping district and carries about 10,000 vehicles on a typical day.

The city’s posted detour will send Plainfield-bound traffic up Seminary Hill to Interstate 89 north and Exit 20. Drivers traveling the opposite direction are directed to I-89 south, Exit 19 and Miracle Mile. Officials are urging motorists to use the signed route instead of smaller local roads, which became congested during an emergency closure in March 2025.

Pedestrians and bicyclists will retain access through a temporary footbridge next to the construction site, although cyclists are encouraged to dismount while crossing. The closure gives contractors room to remove the deteriorated 145-foot bridge and start building its replacement. Because the span also serves buses, emergency vehicles, workers and shoppers, the advance notice and temporary crossing are intended to reduce the disruption that accompanied last year’s sudden shutdown.
dek: The 77-year-old Route 12A span closes Monday for demolition and replacement, redirecting roughly 10,000 daily vehicles to Interstate 89.
headline: West Lebanon dry bridge closes Monday for yearlong replacement

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Boston College marked the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks with its annual Red Bandanna Game, honoring alumnus Welles Crowther during Friday night’s 28-21 football victory over Rutgers. The matchup carried a connection for both universities: Crowther graduated from Boston College, while Rutgers commemorated 37 alumni killed in the attacks.

Crowther, a former Boston College lacrosse player and volunteer firefighter, helped people escape the World Trade Center’s South Tower before he died. Survivors remembered the red bandanna covering his face as he guided them through smoke and returned to help others, giving the cloth lasting significance in the school’s memorial tradition.

Boston College players wore red-and-white paisley elements and “For Welles” on their uniforms. Rutgers incorporated the number 37 and American flag details into its tribute. Fans at Alumni Stadium also carried red bandannas and participated in a coordinated whiteout. The 2026 game was held on September 11 itself, giving the established campus tradition added meaning while linking the schools’ remembrance to service, courage and the alumni communities affected by the attacks.
dek: Boston College and Rutgers used uniforms and stadium tributes to remember Welles Crowther and alumni killed in the September 11 attacks.
headline: Boston College honors Welles Crowther in Red Bandanna Game

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Massachusetts state Sen. William Brownsberger retained the Democratic nomination in the Suffolk and Middlesex district after a two-day recount left him 35 votes ahead of challenger Daniel Lander. The hand count covered more than 24,000 ballots and changed the incumbent’s advantage by one vote from the unofficial 34-vote margin.

Brownsberger has represented the district since 2012 and serves in the state Senate’s leadership. The district includes Belmont, Watertown and portions of Boston and Cambridge. Lander, a former Boston City Hall aide, carried Boston, Watertown and the district’s Cambridge precincts, while Brownsberger’s performance in Belmont supplied the margin that preserved his lead.

Both campaigns requested recounts after the close September 1 primary. Election workers reviewed paper ballots across the four municipalities, with campaign representatives and public observers present. Lander congratulated Brownsberger after the count, and Brownsberger said he was ready to return to work for the district. The certified result moves the contest into the November general election and closes one of the narrowest Massachusetts legislative primaries of the 2026 cycle.
dek: A two-day hand count of more than 24,000 ballots changed the incumbent senator’s advantage by one vote, leaving a 35-vote margin.
headline: Brownsberger keeps Massachusetts Senate nomination by 35 votes

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The National Weather Service has issued a Flood Watch for Rhode Island and southeastern Massachusetts on Sunday as a warm front and weak area of low pressure approach Southern New England. Forecasters say showers may arrive around sunrise and produce pockets of torrential rain through the morning and into the afternoon.

A few thunderstorms are possible, and the heaviest downpours could overwhelm urban drainage or flood other low-lying, poorly drained locations. The Weather Service’s Saturday morning discussion emphasized that conditions may vary over short distances, making the placement of the most intense rain important for local impacts. Storm Team 10 said at least an inch of rain was possible across much of Connecticut and parts of Rhode Island.

Saturday remains the better day for outdoor plans, with sunshine, low humidity and afternoon temperatures in the 70s. Clouds increase overnight before humidity rises sharply Sunday. Rain should taper later Sunday, with any lingering showers departing early Monday. Residents traveling during the watch period should monitor updated forecasts and avoid driving through water covering a roadway.
dek: Forecasters expect showers, possible thunderstorms and pockets of torrential rain from early Sunday into the afternoon.
headline: Flood Watch covers Rhode Island for Sunday downpours

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Providence’s police union is seeking clarity about its future relationship with Democratic mayoral nominee David Morales after his primary victory over incumbent Mayor Brett Smiley. Fraternal Order of Police President Michael Imondi said the union and nominee had not yet spoken and raised questions about staffing, resources and support for officers.

Imondi told NBC 10 that nearly 100 officers could leave the department during the next year. That figure is the union president’s estimate, not an announced departure count. The department currently has about 450 officers, according to the report, making retention and response capacity central concerns as city leadership prepares for a possible transition.

Morales said he wants rank-and-file officers to know that he would listen to their concerns and work with them on community safety. He also said he looked forward to a conversation with police leadership. During the campaign, Morales stepped back from earlier calls to defund the police. The nomination does not decide the office: Morales will face Republican Dave Talan in the November general election. A meeting between the nominee and union would be the first step toward defining how they might work together.
dek: The union president raised staffing concerns while Democratic nominee David Morales said he wants to listen to officers and work with them.
headline: Providence police union seeks dialogue with Morales after primary win

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The White House is considering whether to use the Defense Production Act to expand U.S. oil-refining capacity as elevated fuel costs increase pressure on the domestic energy system, Reuters reported, citing people familiar with the discussions. No final decision has been made, and further talks with refiners are expected.

The discussions are focused on improving efficiency and adding capacity at existing facilities rather than relying only on the construction of entirely new refineries, which can take years and require large capital commitments. Reuters reported that U.S. refining utilization has been running near 98%, leaving limited room to increase output through higher operating rates alone.

The administration is also evaluating permitting changes, regulatory steps and investment incentives. The Defense Production Act can give the federal government tools to prioritize contracts and support production considered important to national security, but any specific application to refining would depend on the policy ultimately selected. The review is developing against the backdrop of disrupted Middle East energy flows and higher transportation costs. Until an action is announced, the proposal remains one option under consideration rather than a new requirement for the industry.
dek: Officials are considering tools to improve and expand existing facilities, but Reuters reports that no final decision has been made.
headline: White House weighs Defense Production Act for refinery expansion

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Chinese President Xi Jinping urged BRICS members to take a peacemaking role in the Middle East war during an address to the bloc’s leaders in New Delhi on Saturday. Xi said the conflict does not serve the international community and that China would work with other members on efforts aimed at peace.

The appeal came as BRICS leaders tried to bridge divisions between Iran and the United Arab Emirates, both members of the expanded group but positioned differently in the regional conflict. Their summit agenda includes diplomacy, economic cooperation and the bloc’s effort to increase the influence of emerging and developing nations in global institutions.

Xi also said China will take over the BRICS chairmanship in 2027 and host the organization’s 19th summit. The group now includes Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa, Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Iran and the UAE. Xi’s remarks do not establish a peace process on their own, but they signal that Middle East diplomacy has become a central test of whether the expanded bloc can coordinate across competing national interests. Further summit statements and bilateral meetings are expected as the gathering continues.
dek: The Chinese president called for a peace role as the expanded bloc navigates differences between Iran and the United Arab Emirates.
headline: Xi urges BRICS to pursue peacemaking role in Middle East war

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Authorities in Mexico’s Puebla state are investigating a clandestine cryptocurrency-mining operation discovered near hydroelectric infrastructure in the Sierra Norte mountains. Reuters reports that investigators found 300 graphics processing units, 80 medium-voltage terminals and eight satellite antennas inside a remote building in Tlaola.

The power demand and mechanical noise helped draw attention to the site. Authorities suspect the operation may have drawn electricity without authorization from infrastructure linked to a nearby dam and may have been used to generate virtual assets for laundering illicit funds. Mexico’s federal attorney general’s office declined to comment because the investigation remains active, so responsibility for the site has not been established publicly.

The Tlaola site is the fourth crypto farm uncovered in that area since early 2025, according to Reuters. The case illustrates how specialized computing hardware, satellite connectivity and stolen energy can be combined in financial crime schemes far from conventional data centers. Blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis estimated that addresses tied to illicit activity received $154 billion globally in 2025, more than double the prior year, with sanctions evasion accounting for much of the increase.
dek: Investigators found 300 GPUs, medium-voltage equipment and satellite antennas at a remote site suspected of taking power from nearby infrastructure.
headline: Mexican crypto-mining raid uncovers 300 GPUs near hydro system

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Ford is recalling 223,472 F-150 pickup trucks in the United States because fuel tanks may leak or separate from the vehicle while it is moving, according to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration. The action covers certain trucks from model years 2023 through 2027.

The safety agency said some tanks may be improperly secured. A detached tank can become a road hazard and increase crash risk, while leaking fuel can cause an engine stall or create a fire risk. The notice does not mean every truck in the model-year range has the defect; owners will be notified based on the vehicles included in Ford’s recall population.

Dealers will inspect the fuel-tank straps and replace them when necessary at no charge, NHTSA said. Owners should use their vehicle identification number with the federal recall database or contact a Ford dealer to determine whether a specific truck is affected and to arrange service after notices are issued. The recall highlights how a relatively basic mounting component can create several connected safety problems, from loss of propulsion to debris on the road and exposure to leaking fuel.
dek: Certain 2023-2027 F-150 trucks may have leaking or improperly secured tanks that can stall an engine, create a road hazard or raise fire risk.
headline: Ford recalls 223,472 F-150 trucks over fuel-tank risk

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: U.S. consumer prices rose 0.4% in August after a 0.1% increase in July, the Labor Department reported Friday. The Consumer Price Index was 3.4% higher than a year earlier, matching July’s annual rate and meeting economists’ expectations for the monthly change.

Core prices, which exclude food and energy, increased 0.3% for the month. Reuters described that as the largest rise in four months, with airline fares continuing their upward trend. The report arrived one day after firm producer-price readings and strengthened the view that underlying inflation pressure persisted despite the unchanged year-over-year headline rate.

Investors responded by increasing expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise its benchmark rate at the September 15-16 policy meeting. That market pricing was a reaction recorded after the report, not a live forecast. The central bank’s target range stood at 3.50% to 3.75% when Reuters published its analysis. For households and businesses, the data reinforce the possibility that borrowing costs will remain restrictive as policymakers assess energy shocks, employment conditions and whether price increases are spreading beyond fuel-related categories.
dek: The monthly CPI increase matched expectations, while a 0.3% rise in core prices reinforced expectations of tighter Federal Reserve policy.
headline: August U.S. inflation rises 0.4% as rate-hike expectations strengthen

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: QatarEnergy is negotiating multiyear agreements for U.S. liquefied natural gas through 2031 as it works to replace supply capacity damaged by Iranian attacks, Reuters reported, citing trading and industry sources. The discussions involve major American LNG producers and mark a shift from short-term spot purchases toward longer coverage.

Damage at Qatar’s Ras Laffan facilities has sidelined about 12.8 million metric tons of annual LNG capacity, according to the report, and repairs could take as long as five years. QatarEnergy Trading is seeking roughly 2 million to 3 million metric tons a year from U.S. projects, providing a potentially significant new source of demand for uncontracted American output.

The negotiations matter beyond Qatar because Asian customers receive about 80% of its LNG exports and are also examining alternative supplies. Longer U.S. contracts could help QatarEnergy meet existing commitments while infrastructure is repaired and shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remains constrained. No completed contract or transaction price was reported, so the talks represent a developing supply strategy rather than a finalized purchase. Their duration nevertheless signals that the company is preparing for disruption that may persist well beyond the current spot market.
dek: The energy company is pursuing multiyear American supply as damaged facilities sideline about 12.8 million metric tons of annual LNG capacity.
headline: QatarEnergy seeks U.S. LNG contracts through 2031

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Lewis Hamilton and Oliver Bearman both crashed during final practice for Formula One’s Spanish Grand Prix at Madrid’s new Madring circuit, interrupting the last track session before Saturday qualifying. Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli finished fastest, with Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc next on the timing sheet.

Hamilton locked his Ferrari at the final corner and hit the barriers with a little more than half an hour remaining. He initially tried to drive the damaged car toward the pits with its front wing trapped underneath and a punctured right-front tire, then stopped after repeated instructions from the team. The session was red-flagged while crews repaired the barrier. Bearman later brought another stoppage when he crashed his Haas near the end.

The incidents added uncertainty before qualifying on a layout where close walls and higher speeds leave little margin for error. Drivers have also said overtaking may be difficult, increasing the importance of grid position for Sunday’s race. Antonelli’s pace gave Mercedes a strong final-practice marker, but the disrupted session limited representative running for several teams as they prepared their qualifying setups.
dek: The two crashes interrupted the final session at the new Madring circuit, where Kimi Antonelli set the fastest practice time.
headline: Hamilton and Bearman crash as Antonelli leads Spanish GP practice

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: England completed a 3-0 Test-series sweep of Pakistan with an eight-wicket victory at Edgbaston, reaching a target of 130 behind unbeaten half-centuries from captain Joe Root and Jordan Cox. Root finished on 62 and Cox on 59 as the hosts closed out the final match after an early wobble in the chase.

Pakistan briefly created pressure with two quick wickets and nearly dismissed Root when he was bowled on a delivery ruled a no-ball. Root and Cox then settled the innings and carried England to the result without another loss. Pakistan had forced England to bat again after a resilient second innings led by debutant Razaullah, who struck 81 from the lower order.

The sweep gave England its first Test-series victory in 19 months and a successful return to captaincy for Root following Ben Stokes’ retirement. England’s bowlers had controlled much of the series, with Ollie Robinson taking 21 wickets. The result offers momentum before a more demanding tour of South Africa, while Pakistan leaves the series looking for greater stability after personnel and coaching changes during a difficult run of results.
dek: Unbeaten half-centuries from Joe Root and Jordan Cox completed an eight-wicket win at Edgbaston and England’s first Test-series victory in 19 months.
headline: Root guides England to 3-0 Test sweep of Pakistan

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The Mark Stebbins Community Center has opened on Manchester’s West Side, bringing youth programs, health care and family services together in one building. The Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Manchester and Amoskeag Health are anchor tenants, creating a shared location for services that had previously operated through separate organizations.

The center will offer after-school programming, affordable health care, a food pantry, meeting space, community navigators and referrals to other nonprofit support. Its fundraising campaign collected $20.7 million, exceeding an $18.5 million goal after the Catholic Health Care Foundation of Greater Manchester announced a $1 million pledge. The total includes an endowment intended to support long-term operations and maintenance.

The Manchester Housing and Redevelopment Authority provided roughly three acres through a 75-year lease priced at $10 a year, according to remarks at the opening. Federal Community Project Funding secured through the Department of Housing and Urban Development also supported the project. Named for the late businessman and philanthropist Mark Stebbins, the center reflects his goal of helping West Side children and families through coordinated services. With construction complete, the measure of success now shifts from fundraising to how consistently residents can reach and use those programs.
dek: The $20.7 million center combines youth programs, health care, a food pantry and nonprofit support under one roof.
headline: Mark Stebbins Community Center opens on Manchester’s West Side

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The Upper Valley Haven is preparing to open a 20-bed, year-round emergency shelter and daytime resource center in White River Junction, expanding services for people across the New Hampshire-Vermont border region. The Patrick and Marcelle Leahy Shelter and Resource Center at 608 North Main Street is expected to welcome its first guests in the coming weeks.

The facility replaces a seasonal shelter in Lebanon, New Hampshire, that offered 14 beds for roughly three months each winter. That building is slated for demolition as part of a roundabout project. During its most recent season, 66 people stayed for a combined total of about 100 nights, while an average of two people per night were turned away because space was unavailable.

The Haven raised $10.2 million for the new center and expects it to provide about 5,000 overnight stays annually for roughly 100 people. Year-round operation is intended to reduce weather-driven gaps and connect guests with support during daytime hours. For New Hampshire communities in the Upper Valley, the opening adds nearby capacity as local providers contend with persistent housing insecurity and limited emergency beds.
dek: The 20-bed center in White River Junction will replace a smaller seasonal Lebanon shelter and serve the broader cross-border region.
headline: Upper Valley Haven readies year-round shelter serving New Hampshire region
location: Upper Valley, New Hampshire and Vermont

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Former Fall River Mayor Jasiel Correia has agreed to pay $170 a month toward more than $306,000 in outstanding restitution after completing his federal prison sentence in July. The payment schedule appears in federal court documents filed this week and can be reviewed as his financial circumstances change.

Correia was convicted in 2021 on public-corruption charges and received a six-year prison sentence. He had been ordered to pay more than $310,000 in restitution. The new plan reflects his current employment and reported finances rather than reducing the amount owed. Federal probation officials can periodically reassess his ability to pay and seek adjustments to the monthly figure.

Court filings identify Correia’s current job as a full-time marketing manager at the Towne House. Restitution plans are intended to keep repayment active after incarceration while allowing supervision officials to account for a defendant’s income and expenses. The case remains a prominent chapter in Fall River politics because the criminal conduct occurred while Correia held office. The latest filing sets the immediate repayment terms but leaves open the possibility of higher installments if his financial position improves.
dek: Federal filings show Jasiel Correia still owes more than $306,000, with the payment amount subject to periodic review.
headline: Former Fall River mayor begins $170 monthly restitution plan

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The New England Patriots have placed wide receiver A.J. Brown on injured reserve after he sustained a high ankle sprain in his debut with the team. The roster move means Brown must miss at least four games, turning what had been a week-to-week injury question into a defined early-season absence.

Brown left the game in the third quarter and did not return. High ankle sprains can limit a receiver’s acceleration, cutting and ability to absorb contact, making recovery timelines particularly important for a player expected to carry a large share of the passing game. The injured-reserve designation gives Brown additional time to rehabilitate without occupying an active roster spot.

New England will now have to redistribute targets and snaps while its new star receiver is unavailable. The four-game minimum does not guarantee Brown will return as soon as he is eligible; his progress will determine when the team activates him. The transaction is a significant change from the immediate uncertainty after the injury and gives the Patriots a clearer planning window for the next portion of their schedule.
dek: The high ankle sprain suffered in Brown’s Patriots debut will sideline the star receiver for at least four games.
headline: Patriots place A.J. Brown on injured reserve

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Former U.S. Representative Jim Langevin is urging stronger oversight of artificial intelligence as Rhode Island expands education and policy work around the technology. Langevin, now the distinguished chair of the Institute for Cybersecurity and Emerging Technologies at Rhode Island College, said safeguards and transparency should keep pace with rapid adoption.

Langevin led Rhode Island’s AI task force, which released recommendations earlier this year. He is also considering joining a government advisory board at OpenAI, according to NBC 10 News. His comments place the state’s debate within a broader national discussion over how governments should address risks without closing off useful applications in education, public services and business.

Rhode Island College’s cybersecurity and emerging-technologies program now serves more than 500 students, giving the policy discussion a local workforce dimension. Langevin’s position combines experience in Congress with the institute’s focus on training and research. No specific new Rhode Island regulation was announced, but his call adds momentum to efforts to translate task-force recommendations into practical rules. The central question is how to require accountability from developers and users while preserving room for responsible innovation.
dek: The former congressman says transparency and safeguards should advance alongside AI adoption and workforce training.
headline: Jim Langevin calls for stronger AI oversight in Rhode Island

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The University of Rhode Island football team opens its Pawtucket home schedule Saturday against Elon in a noon kickoff at Centreville Bank Stadium. URI is billing the game as its Welcome Back event for the campus community, with the Rams beginning another season after winning consecutive Coastal Athletic Association championships.

The Pawtucket setting gives the program a different home-stage atmosphere while its usual Kingston venue undergoes major work. URI is offering discounted admission to faculty and staff, and the event is designed to reconnect students and employees with the team at the start of the academic year. The university advised attendees to review stadium information before traveling.

Elon provides an immediate conference-level test for a Rhode Island team carrying higher expectations after back-to-back titles. An opening game can also reveal how quickly new starters and adjusted units have settled into their roles. The noon start makes transportation and arrival planning especially relevant for supporters traveling from Kingston and elsewhere in the state. Saturday’s result will offer the first competitive measure of URI’s bid to sustain its recent run of success.
dek: The back-to-back CAA champion Rams begin their season against Elon at Centreville Bank Stadium in Pawtucket.
headline: URI opens Pawtucket home slate against Elon

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: A planned Monday meeting between Iran and Gulf states in Oman is expected to cover the Strait of Hormuz but is unlikely to produce a signed agreement, a senior Iranian official told Reuters. The assessment tempers expectations around talks focused on one of the world’s most consequential shipping routes.

Iran has spent months negotiating with Oman and says it plans to attend the gathering. Oman has not formally announced the meeting, while other invited governments have remained largely silent; Bahrain has said it will not participate. Tehran has sought fees from vessels using the strait, a proposal Oman rejects, leaving a central point of disagreement unresolved before delegates meet.

Roughly one-fifth of global oil supplies moved through Hormuz before the war that began in February, making any change in access important to energy markets and shipping costs. Oil prices surged during the past week as regional risks intensified. The official’s comments indicate that Monday may function as a negotiating step rather than a deadline. Confirmation of attendance, the meeting’s agenda and any practical navigation arrangements remain the key developments to watch.
dek: A senior Iranian official described Monday’s Oman meeting as a negotiating step, with major disagreements over the strategic waterway unresolved.
headline: Iran says Oman talks unlikely to produce signed Hormuz deal

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar said Saturday that his government will change a 2020 adoption rule that effectively barred gay and lesbian couples from adopting children. The announcement marks a significant policy reversal after Magyar defeated former Prime Minister Viktor Orban in April, ending Orban’s 16 years in power.

Before the 2020 law, one partner in a same-sex couple could apply to adopt as a single person. The Orban-era measure required single applicants to obtain approval from the family affairs minister, creating what Reuters described as an effective ban. Magyar said adoption decisions should be made by qualified professionals rather than a politician, though he did not provide a timetable or legislative text.

Hungary recognizes civil unions but does not allow same-sex marriage. The European Court of Justice ruled in April that separate Hungarian restrictions on LGBTQ content violated European law. Rewriting the adoption process would therefore become an early test of the new government’s approach to civil rights and its relationship with European institutions. The next concrete steps are the introduction of legislation and details about how professional adoption reviews would operate.
dek: Prime Minister Peter Magyar announced a reversal of the 2020 system but did not yet provide legislation or a timetable.
headline: Hungary moves to reverse restriction on gay adoption

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei is calling on leading artificial-intelligence companies to deliberately slow the rate at which their models gain new capabilities. The proposal, reported by Reuters, frames pacing as a way to preserve time for governments, researchers and companies to manage risks before systems advance further.

Amodei outlined a three-step framework rather than advocating a halt to development. His argument is that even moderated progress would remain rapid, while a more controlled cadence could improve evaluation, safeguards and public preparation. The recommendation arrives as major labs compete to release more capable agents and reasoning systems, with capital spending and product plans increasingly tied to short model cycles.

The appeal does not itself create a binding industry standard, and rivals have not committed to a shared slowdown. Coordinated pacing would also raise practical questions about measurement, enforcement and international competition. Still, a chief executive asking peers to constrain capability growth adds a notable voice to the safety debate. The next signal will be whether Anthropic changes its own release schedule or turns the framework into specific technical and governance commitments.
dek: Dario Amodei outlined a framework for moderating capability gains so safeguards and public preparation have more time to catch up.
headline: Anthropic CEO urges slower AI capability growth

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: India should create a forum that helps its technology companies engage foreign governments and regulators as they expand abroad, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said. The proposed platform would let companies coordinate before overseas regulatory positions harden and market barriers become more difficult to change.

Indian firms are entering markets where governments are writing rules for agentic artificial intelligence, tokenized assets, data handling and cybersecurity. Sitharaman argued that a young startup cannot reasonably be expected to understand and negotiate every regulatory system by itself. A shared forum could pool expertise, identify compatible standards and help companies address policy questions before launching products in a new jurisdiction.

The proposal could also support licensing, partnerships and revenue from Indian technology overseas, though no launch date, governance structure or membership rules were announced. Its value would depend on whether it represents a broad mix of startups and established companies without becoming a substitute for each firm’s compliance work. As technology regulation diverges across countries, coordinated engagement may reduce duplicated effort. The next step is for India to turn the concept into an operating body with clear authority and channels to foreign regulators.
dek: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman says a shared platform could help startups navigate foreign rules on AI, data and cybersecurity.
headline: India proposes forum to help tech firms navigate global regulation

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: HDFC Bank’s board has submitted two candidates to the Reserve Bank of India for approval as the private lender’s next chief executive, Reuters reported. The candidates were not named. The selection will determine the successor to Sashidhar Jagdishan, who is scheduled to retire when his second term ends in October.

Indian private banks must obtain the central bank’s prior approval before appointing a chief executive, giving the regulator a direct role in the succession. HDFC Bank has also reappointed V. Srinivasa Rangan as a whole-time director and named Jimmy Tata to the same type of position. The incoming CEO is expected to fill a fourth whole-time director role.

Leadership continuity matters for HDFC Bank because of its scale and the operational demands of its expanded franchise. The board’s submission moves the process into the regulatory phase but does not indicate which candidate is preferred or when the RBI will decide. Investors will be watching for the nominee’s priorities on growth, asset quality and integration. Until approval is announced, the bank’s existing leadership remains responsible for managing the transition toward Jagdishan’s October departure.
dek: The unnamed nominees require Reserve Bank of India approval before Sashidhar Jagdishan’s second term ends in October.
headline: HDFC Bank submits two CEO candidates to India’s central bank

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The U.S. Commerce Department has finalized steep antidumping and countervailing duties on solar cells and panels imported from India, Indonesia and Laos. The decision advances a trade case brought by an alliance of domestic manufacturers that includes First Solar, Hanwha Qcells and Mission Solar.

Final antidumping margins were set at 123.04% for India, 94.36% for Indonesia and 65.43% for Laos. Countervailing-duty rates were 126.09% for India, ranged from 73.2% to 173.7% for Indonesia, and ranged from 82.03% to 153.67% for Laos. The rates address separate findings on below-market pricing and government subsidies, and actual importer liability can vary by company and product.

The case now moves to the U.S. International Trade Commission, which is expected to make a final injury determination by October 14. If the commission finds that the imports harmed or threatened domestic producers, formal duty orders would follow in November. The outcome could alter sourcing costs and project planning across the U.S. solar industry, balancing domestic manufacturing goals against developers’ need for competitively priced equipment. No final orders take effect unless the injury finding is affirmative.
dek: Solar imports from India, Indonesia and Laos face triple-digit rates in some cases, pending a final U.S. injury determination.
headline: U.S. finalizes steep duties on Asian solar imports

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Ducati rider Marc Marquez won the San Marino Grand Prix sprint Saturday, beating Aprilia’s Marco Bezzecchi and cutting Jorge Martin’s MotoGP championship lead to 14 points. Martin finished third, keeping the title fight compressed ahead of Sunday’s full-distance race.

Bezzecchi started from pole after setting a lap record, but Marquez moved ahead at the first turn and controlled the 13-lap sprint. He reinforced the performance with a race-lap record on the penultimate tour. Bezzecchi’s runner-up finish leaves him 22 points behind Martin in third place in the standings, preserving a three-rider contest near the top.

Sprint points have made Saturdays increasingly important in MotoGP, and Marquez converted track position into a material championship gain without waiting for the main event. The result also demonstrated Ducati’s race pace against Aprilia’s qualifying speed. Sunday will offer more points and a longer strategic test, with tire management and launch execution likely to matter. For now, Marquez’s victory ensures the San Marino weekend will tighten rather than settle the title picture.
dek: The Ducati rider beat Marco Bezzecchi over 13 laps and moved within 14 points of MotoGP leader Jorge Martin.
headline: Marc Marquez wins San Marino sprint to tighten title race

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Brielle Saracini marked the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks by throwing a ceremonial first pitch at Yankee Stadium, accompanied by retired captain Derek Jeter. The appearance renewed a bond that began after Saracini lost her father, Victor, the pilot of hijacked United Airlines Flight 175, when the plane struck the World Trade Center’s South Tower.

Saracini was a young Yankees fan when she first met Jeter, and their connection continued through milestones in her life. She later met her husband, Sean McGuire, at a camp for children who had lost a parent in the attacks. Their shared experience became part of a family story shaped by grief, remembrance and long-term support.

The first pitch placed a personal history inside a public commemoration, linking a New York sports institution with one family’s path over a quarter-century. Jeter’s presence reflected the value of relationships that continued long after the immediate aftermath. For Saracini, the moment honored her father while also showing the life built since his death. The ceremony offered a quieter measure of September 11’s legacy: connections sustained across generations, not only anniversaries.
dek: Brielle Saracini’s ceremonial first pitch renewed a bond formed after her father, Flight 175 pilot Victor Saracini, died in the attacks.
headline: Yankees fan honors father alongside Derek Jeter 25 years after September 11

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Concord High’s defense controlled Friday night’s game in Hudson, helping the Crimson Tide defeat Alvirne 37-7. The game remained scoreless until the final 34 seconds of the first half, but Concord broke it open after halftime with two touchdowns and a safety in the third quarter.

The Crimson Tide finished with 15 tackles for loss, six sacks and a fumble recovery. Jax Diachenko led the pressure with 3.5 sacks, three tackles for loss and the safety. Sebastian Telus added five tackles for loss and two sacks, while Michael Gamache contributed three tackles for loss and a half-sack. Dustin Ellis forced and recovered a fumble.

On offense, Colin Savard carried 21 times for 176 yards. Quarterback Rhys Craigue completed eight of 19 passes for 142 yards, including an 11-yard touchdown to Methuselah Doe. A 50-yard gain by Savard on a short reception helped set up that score. Concord’s combination of backfield disruption and a steady rushing attack turned a tight first half into a decisive road victory.
dek: The Crimson Tide recorded 15 tackles for loss and six sacks before pulling away with two touchdowns and a safety in the third quarter.
headline: Concord defense powers 37-7 win over Alvirne

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Two young New Hampshire cattle handlers turned years of practice into ribbons at the 2026 Hopkinton State Fair. Molly Potter and Rose DeFreitas showed four steers after learning to work with cattle together at a summer camp run by Miles Smith Farm in 2022.

Their preparation extended well beyond fair week. The pair worked with the animals through winter and spring, teaching them to walk calmly, respond to direction and remain composed around crowds. The calves came from Huckins Farm in Bristol, and the project required the students to build trust with animals much larger than they are.

Potter comes from a family with deep agricultural roots and is described as a 13th-generation farmer. DeFreitas developed her interest through the farm program and the partnership the two formed there. Their showing results reflected both technical handling and months of daily care. The experience also demonstrated how fairs connect young people with working agriculture: the ribbons are the visible result, but patience, safety and consistency are the skills developed long before an animal enters the ring.
dek: Molly Potter and Rose DeFreitas brought four steers to the 2026 fair after building their skills through farm camp and year-round training.
headline: Young handlers turn years of cattle training into Hopkinton Fair ribbons

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: An off-duty Sandwich police officer was arrested after a suspected impaired-driving crash in the Forestdale section of town Friday night, according to the department. Police identified the officer as Matthew Cotter, 44, and said no injuries were reported.

Authorities said an SUV traveled through bushes and hit a parked vehicle on Grand Oak Road at about 9:30 p.m. Responding Sandwich officers believed the driver showed signs of impairment and called Massachusetts State Police to handle the investigation because the suspect was a member of the local department. State police then arrested Cotter on OUI-related charges.

Sandwich police placed Cotter on administrative leave and opened an internal investigation. He is expected to be arraigned in Barnstable District Court; information about an attorney was not immediately available. Police also said a separate investigation was opened after a relative at the scene allegedly became verbally abusive and assaultive toward a news photographer. The allegations in both matters remain subject to investigation and court review.
dek: State police arrested Matthew Cotter after an SUV went through bushes and struck a parked vehicle in Forestdale, local police said.
headline: Off-duty Sandwich officer arrested after suspected OUI crash

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: A round of heavy rain is expected to move through Massachusetts on Sunday morning, prompting flood watches for parts of the state from late Saturday night into Sunday afternoon. Forecasters said the system could produce localized flash flooding and ponding on roads, especially where downpours repeatedly cross the same area.

The rain is expected to arrive from west to east overnight and become most widespread during the morning. Isolated thunderstorms are possible, although the threat of severe weather was described as low. Drivers should be prepared for reduced visibility, standing water and slower travel during the wettest periods.

Conditions are forecast to improve from west to east during the early to middle part of Sunday afternoon. Temperatures should remain in the lower 70s, held down by clouds and rain. The precise placement of the heaviest bands will determine which communities see the greatest flooding risk, so residents should monitor updated local alerts and avoid driving through water covering a roadway.
dek: Forecasters expect the heaviest rain Sunday morning, with localized flash flooding and roadway ponding possible before conditions improve.
headline: Flood watches posted as heavy Sunday rain approaches Massachusetts

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: A 22-year-old man from Foster died after his motorcycle collided with a tow truck on Tunk Hill Road in Scituate late Friday, police said. The crash occurred at about 10 p.m. and closed the road while emergency crews and investigators worked at the scene.

According to a witness account relayed by police, the motorcycle was traveling west when a tow truck began leaving a driveway with its emergency lights activated. The rider was unable to stop before striking the truck. He was pronounced dead at the scene. Authorities had not released his name as of Saturday morning.

The tow-truck operator was taken to a hospital for treatment. Police said their preliminary investigation indicates speed may have contributed to the collision, but no final determination has been announced. The investigation remains active. The new details identify the fatal outcome of the police response that drew a large presence to Tunk Hill Road Friday night.
dek: Police said the motorcycle collided with a tow truck exiting a driveway on Tunk Hill Road late Friday night.
headline: Foster motorcyclist, 22, killed in Scituate crash

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Seven people, including a Providence police officer, were taken to hospitals after a four-vehicle crash late Friday at Thurbers and Prairie avenues, police said. The collision began while the officer was responding to a service call.

According to Providence police, another car struck the cruiser and triggered a chain reaction that pulled two additional vehicles into the crash. The officer was treated and later released from the hospital. Six other occupants were hospitalized with complaints of pain; authorities did not report more detailed information about their conditions.

The intersection is near major routes through the southern part of the city, and the late-night response brought police and medical crews to the area. Investigators have not announced whether citations or charges are expected, and no cause beyond the initial sequence of impacts has been released. Police said the investigation remains ongoing. The number of vehicles and patients makes the incident one of the larger traffic responses reported in Providence overnight.
dek: A cruiser responding to a service call was struck at Thurbers and Prairie avenues, setting off a crash involving four vehicles.
headline: Seven hospitalized after Providence police-cruiser chain crash

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: BRICS leaders unanimously adopted the New Delhi Declaration on Saturday, expressing deep concern about the Middle East war and calling for maximum restraint. The formal adoption converts an earlier agreement among negotiators into the 10-member group’s official summit position.

The statement advocates a multilateral approach that respects national viewpoints and reiterates support for settling international disputes through dialogue, consultation and diplomacy. Reaching consensus carried added significance because the expanded bloc includes both Iran and the United Arab Emirates, a close U.S. partner, while the United States and Iran have resumed exchanges of strikes after an August pause.

The declaration also raised concern about unilateral tariff and non-tariff measures that distort trade, against a backdrop of U.S. sanctions on Iran and Russia. BRICS now includes Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa, Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Iran and the UAE. The declaration provides a common diplomatic text, but implementation will depend on whether members can translate broad calls for restraint into coordinated action.
dek: The 10-member bloc urged maximum restraint and peaceful dispute resolution despite sharp differences among members over the conflict.
headline: BRICS unanimously adopts New Delhi declaration on Middle East war

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: A federal judge has ruled that the administration acted unlawfully by directing the Federal Emergency Management Agency to cut its workforce in half. U.S. District Judge Susan Illston said the Department of Homeland Security improperly took over FEMA’s authority over its personnel and steered the agency toward eliminating thousands of disaster-response jobs.

The late-Friday decision cited a federal law enacted after Hurricane Katrina that bars DHS from substantially reducing FEMA’s authorities, responsibilities or functions. Illston agreed with unions challenging the cuts that the department violated the law when it moved to stop FEMA from renewing temporary contracts for on-call reservists who respond to disasters.

The ruling does not yet impose a remedy or penalty. The judge said the scope of relief will be addressed separately next month after additional briefing. She also noted that FEMA projected staffing of 11,383 for the coming fiscal year, roughly half its prior level, without a documented basis for that number. FEMA, DHS and the largest federal-worker union did not immediately comment Saturday.
dek: The court found that Homeland Security overstepped FEMA’s control of its personnel; remedies will be considered separately next month.
headline: Federal judge rules plan to halve FEMA workforce unlawful

author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Users located in Houthi-held northern Yemen attempted to use Anthropic’s Claude artificial-intelligence system to develop advanced missile technology, the company said in a new threat report.
